title: The continuous spectrum of bound states in expulsive potentials
summary: On the contrary to the common intuition that a steep expulsive potential makes quantum states widely delocalized, we demonstrate that one- and two-dimensional (1D and 2D) Schrödinger equations, which include expulsive potentials that are \emph{steeper than the quadratic} (anti-harmonic-oscillator) ones, give rise to \emph{normalizable} (effectively localized) eigenstates. These states constitute full continuous spectra in the 1D and 2D cases alike. In 1D, these are spatially even and odd eigenstates. The 2D states may carry any value of the vorticity (alias magnetic quantum number). Asymptotic approximations for wave functions of the 1D and 2D eigenstates, valid far from the center, are derived analytically, demonstrating excellent agreement with numerically found counterparts. Special exact solutions for vortex states are obtained in the 2D case. These findings suggest an extension of the concept of bound states in the continuum, in quantum mechanics and paraxial photonics. Gross-Pitaevskii equations are considered as the nonlinear extension of the 1D and 2D settings. In 1D, the cubic nonlinearity slightly deforms the eigenstates, maintaining their stability. On the other hand, the quintic self-focusing term, which occurs in the photonic version of the 1D model, initiates the dynamical collapse of states whose norm exceeds a critical value.

AI.tldr: Steeper-than-quadratic expulsive potentials produce normalizable eigenstates with continuous spectra in 1D and 2D quantum systems, extending bound-state concepts and showing nonlinear stability/collapse behavior.
AI.motivation: Challenge the common intuition that steep expulsive potentials only produce delocalized states, and explore whether steeper-than-quadratic potentials can yield normalizable eigenstates with continuous spectra.
AI.method: Analyze 1D and 2D Schrödinger equations with expulsive potentials steeper than quadratic; derive asymptotic approximations for wave functions; obtain special exact solutions for vortex states in 2D; extend to nonlinear Gross-Pitaevskii equations with cubic and quintic terms.
AI.result: Demonstrate that steeper-than-quadratic expulsive potentials produce normalizable eigenstates with full continuous spectra in both 1D and 2D; derive analytical asymptotic approximations showing excellent numerical agreement; obtain exact vortex solutions in 2D; show cubic nonlinearity maintains stability while quintic self-focusing initiates collapse above critical norm.
AI.conclusion: These findings extend the concept of bound states in the continuum, challenging conventional wisdom about localization in steep potentials, with implications for quantum mechanics and paraxial photonics.

title: Encoding Matters: Benchmarking Binary and D-ary Representations for Quantum Combinatorial Optimization
summary: Combinatorial optimization problems are typically formulated using Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO), where constraints are enforced through penalty terms that introduce auxiliary variables and rapidly increase Hamiltonian complexity, limiting scalability on near term quantum devices. In this work, we systematically study Quadratic Unconstrained D-ary Optimization (QUDO) as an alternative formulation in which decision variables are encoded directly in higher dimensional Hilbert spaces. We demonstrate that QUDO naturally captures structural constraints across a range of problem classes, including the Traveling Salesman Problem, two variants of the Vehicle Routing Problem, graph coloring, job scheduling, and Max-K-Cut, without the need for extensive penalty constructions. Using a qudit-level implementation of the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (qudit QAOA), we benchmark these formulations against their binary QUBO counterparts and exact classical solutions. Our study show consistently improved approximation ratios and substantially reduced computational overhead at comparable circuit depths, highlighting QUDO as a scalable and expressive representation for quantum combinatorial optimization.

AI.tldr: QUDO (Quadratic Unconstrained D-ary Optimization) outperforms QUBO for quantum combinatorial optimization by eliminating penalty terms, reducing Hamiltonian complexity, and improving approximation ratios with qudit QAOA.
AI.motivation: QUBO formulations require penalty terms that introduce auxiliary variables and rapidly increase Hamiltonian complexity, limiting scalability on near-term quantum devices. There's a need for more efficient formulations that can capture constraints naturally without extensive penalty constructions.
AI.method: Systematically study QUDO as an alternative formulation where decision variables are encoded directly in higher-dimensional Hilbert spaces. Use qudit-level implementation of QAOA (qudit QAOA) to benchmark QUDO formulations against binary QUBO counterparts and exact classical solutions across multiple problem classes.
AI.result: QUDO naturally captures structural constraints across Traveling Salesman Problem, Vehicle Routing Problem variants, graph coloring, job scheduling, and Max-K-Cut without penalty constructions. QUDO formulations show consistently improved approximation ratios and substantially reduced computational overhead at comparable circuit depths compared to QUBO.
AI.conclusion: QUDO represents a scalable and expressive representation for quantum combinatorial optimization that outperforms traditional QUBO formulations, offering improved performance with reduced complexity on near-term quantum devices.

title: The ABL Rule and the Perils of Post-Selection
summary: In 1964, Aharonov, Bergmann, and Lebowitz introduced their well-known ABL rule with the intention of providing a time-symmetric formalism for computing novel kinds of conditional probabilities in quantum theory. Later papers attached additional significance to the ABL rule, including assertions that it supported violations of the uncertainty principle. The present work challenges these claims, as well as subsequent attempts to salvage the original interpretation of the ABL rule. Taking a broader view, this paper identifies a subtle category error at the heart of the ABL rule that consists of confusing observables that belong to a single system with emergent observables that arise only for physical ensembles. Along the way, this paper points out other problems and fallacious reasoning in the research literature surrounding the ABL rule, including the misuse of post-selection, a reliance on pattern matching to classical formulas, and a posture of measurementism that takes experimental data as providing answers to interpretational questions.

AI.tldr: The paper critiques the ABL rule's interpretation, challenging claims about uncertainty principle violations and identifying a category error in confusing single-system observables with ensemble-based emergent observables.
AI.motivation: To challenge the interpretations and significance attached to the ABL rule, particularly claims about uncertainty principle violations, and to identify fundamental conceptual errors in its application and interpretation.
AI.method: Critical analysis of the ABL rule's foundations, identification of category errors between single-system observables and ensemble-based emergent observables, and examination of fallacious reasoning in the research literature.
AI.result: The paper identifies a fundamental category error at the heart of the ABL rule, challenges claims about uncertainty principle violations, and points out problems including misuse of post-selection, pattern matching to classical formulas, and measurementism.
AI.conclusion: The ABL rule's interpretations are flawed due to conceptual errors, particularly confusing observables belonging to single systems with emergent observables that only arise for physical ensembles, undermining claims about its significance for quantum foundations.

title: Quantum Many-Body Principles of Localized-State Ensemble Luminescence
summary: Localized electron states induced by various disorders,including defects and impurities,usually exist in solids.Their optical properties,especially their luminescence properties,are of both scientific and technological significance.But a microscopic theory has not yet been established for such localized-state ensemble (LSE) luminescence.In this Letter,we attempt to fill this void via developing a quantum many-body (MB) luminescence theory taking into account both electron-phonon (e-p) and electron-electron (e-e) interactions.By using the developed MB-LSE theory,abnormal thermal behaviors such as redshift and subsequent blueshift of peak position,narrowing and succeeding broadening of linewidth,decline in intensity,and variation in lifetime can be quantitatively interpreted.The roles of electron-phonon and electron-electron interactions in the variable-temperature LSE luminescence are thus elucidated. Within the framework of the MB-LSE theory, moreover, Varshni's empirical formula for bandgap temperature dependence and Huang-Rhys factor for e-p coupling are further derived and discussed.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a quantum many-body theory for localized-state ensemble luminescence that explains abnormal thermal behaviors by incorporating both electron-phonon and electron-electron interactions.
AI.motivation: There is no established microscopic theory for localized-state ensemble (LSE) luminescence despite its scientific and technological significance, particularly for understanding optical properties of disordered solids with defects and impurities.
AI.method: Developed a quantum many-body (MB) luminescence theory that incorporates both electron-phonon (e-p) and electron-electron (e-e) interactions to describe LSE luminescence.
AI.result: The MB-LSE theory quantitatively explains abnormal thermal behaviors: redshift then blueshift of peak position, narrowing then broadening of linewidth, intensity decline, and lifetime variation. It also derives Varshni's empirical formula and Huang-Rhys factor.
AI.conclusion: The developed many-body theory successfully fills the theoretical gap for LSE luminescence, elucidates the roles of electron-phonon and electron-electron interactions, and provides a framework that connects to established empirical formulas.

title: Analysis of the Hopfield Model Incorporating the Effects of Unlearning
summary: We analyze a variant of the Hopfield model that incorporates an unlearning mechanism based on spin correlations in the high-temperature regime. In the large system limit where extensively many patterns are stored, we employ the replica method under the replica symmetric ansatz to characterize the model analytically. Our analysis provides a systematic and self-consistent framework that yields order-parameter equations and stability conditions at finite temperatures over a wide range of parameter settings. The resulting theory accurately captures the behavior of the signal-to-noise ratio, the memory capacity, and the criteria for selecting optimal hyperparameters, in agreement with the qualitative findings of Nokura (1996 \textit{J. Phys. A: Math. Gen.} \textbf{29} 3871). Moreover, the theoretical predictions show good agreement with numerical simulations, supporting the conclusion that unlearning enhances memory capacity by suppressing spurious memories.

AI.tldr: Analysis of Hopfield model with high-temperature unlearning mechanism using replica method shows enhanced memory capacity by suppressing spurious memories.
AI.motivation: To understand how unlearning mechanisms based on spin correlations in the high-temperature regime affect memory capacity in Hopfield networks, building on previous work by Nokura (1996).
AI.method: Replica method under replica symmetric ansatz applied to Hopfield model variant with unlearning mechanism; analytical framework yields order-parameter equations and stability conditions at finite temperatures.
AI.result: Theory accurately captures signal-to-noise ratio, memory capacity, and optimal hyperparameter criteria; shows good agreement with numerical simulations; unlearning enhances memory capacity by suppressing spurious memories.
AI.conclusion: Unlearning mechanisms in Hopfield networks systematically improve memory capacity through suppression of spurious memories, with theoretical framework validated by simulations and consistent with prior qualitative findings.

title: Non-Markovianity in a dressed qubit with local dephasing
summary: We study the dynamics of a dressed qubit implemented by a spinless fermion hopping between two lattice sites with each site strongly coupled to a bath of phonons. We employ Lang-Firsov transformation to make the problem tractable perturbatively. Applying time-convolutionless master equation within the polaron frame, we investigate decoherence dynamics of the dressed qubit within the singlet-triplet basis of the system for a wide range of bath spectral densities. It is shown that the coherence persists for longer time scales for large coupling values and shows non-monotonic behaviour reflecting the presence of non-Markovianity in the dynamics. Non-Markovianity, characterized by coherence revivals and non-monotonic decay patterns, emerges distinctly depending on the bath spectrum and coupling strengths. Systems coupled to sub-Ohmic baths, whether both or in combination with another type, display pronounced memory effects at relatively small values of couplings. In contrast, combinations involving Ohmic and super-Ohmic baths exhibit noticeable non-Markovianity only at higher couplings.

AI.tldr: Study of decoherence dynamics in a dressed qubit system (spinless fermion hopping between two sites) strongly coupled to phonon baths, showing non-Markovian coherence revivals and non-monotonic decay patterns dependent on bath spectral densities.
AI.motivation: To understand decoherence dynamics in strongly coupled qubit-phonon systems, particularly how bath spectral densities and coupling strengths affect coherence preservation and non-Markovian memory effects in dressed qubits.
AI.method: Lang-Firsov transformation to make the strongly coupled system tractable, followed by time-convolutionless master equation in the polaron frame to study decoherence dynamics within the singlet-triplet basis for various bath spectral densities.
AI.result: Coherence persists longer for large coupling values with non-monotonic behavior indicating non-Markovianity. Sub-Ohmic baths show pronounced memory effects at small couplings, while Ohmic/super-Ohmic combinations require higher couplings for noticeable non-Markovianity. Coherence revivals and non-monotonic decay patterns emerge depending on bath spectrum.
AI.conclusion: Non-Markovian dynamics in dressed qubits strongly depend on bath spectral densities, with sub-Ohmic baths enhancing memory effects at low couplings and coherence preservation improving with strong coupling, suggesting potential for quantum information applications through bath engineering.

title: Percolation and Threshold-like Behavior in Multiple Sclerosis Progression
summary: In this study we investigate the Percolation Hypothesis for Multiple Sclerosis Progression. The methodology relies on cross-reference analysis centered around a question: What is the evidence for a Percolation/phase-transition hypothesis in Multiple Sclerosis (MS), especially the idea that the RRMS dynamic balance can abruptly break akin to crossing a percolation threshold into SPMS? We identify theoretical models invoking percolation/critical thresholds, network/connectome studies assessing percolation robustness or threshold-like behavior, clinical markers showing thresholds or early-warning signals, and counter-evidence arguing for gradual/continuum transitions.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates the Percolation Hypothesis for Multiple Sclerosis progression, examining evidence for phase-transition dynamics where relapsing-remitting MS can abruptly transition to secondary progressive MS akin to crossing a percolation threshold.
AI.motivation: To systematically evaluate whether Multiple Sclerosis progression follows a percolation/phase-transition model rather than a gradual continuum, particularly examining the hypothesis that the dynamic balance in relapsing-remitting MS can abruptly break into secondary progressive MS when crossing a critical threshold.
AI.method: Cross-reference analysis approach examining four key areas: 1) theoretical models invoking percolation/critical thresholds, 2) network/connectome studies assessing percolation robustness or threshold-like behavior, 3) clinical markers showing thresholds or early-warning signals, and 4) counter-evidence arguing for gradual/continuum transitions.
AI.result: The study identifies and synthesizes evidence from multiple domains supporting the percolation hypothesis, including theoretical frameworks, network connectivity studies, and clinical markers, while also acknowledging counter-evidence suggesting more gradual progression patterns.
AI.conclusion: The percolation hypothesis provides a plausible framework for understanding abrupt transitions in MS progression, particularly the RRMS to SPMS shift, though evidence remains mixed and further research is needed to validate threshold-based models against continuum models.

title: Sensing weak anharmonicities with a passive-active anti-PT symmetric system
summary: We propose a scheme for enhanced sensing of weak anharmonicities based on a three-mode anti-parity-time (anti-PT) symmetric cavity-magnon-waveguide system. By tuning the optical gain to the active cavity mode, the linewidth suppression point for the anti-PT symmetric Hamiltonian can be flexibly controlled even when the two dissipative magnonic modes experience strong intrinsic decay. This essential characteristic is utilized for detecting weak nonlinearities in both the cavity and magnonic modes, with both demonstrating similar high levels of sensitivity. Moreover, the sensitivity can be greatly improved with a detuned laser drive. Based on the integrated passive-active three-mode anti-PT symmetric system, the sensing scheme can be generalized to various physical systems with anharmonicities.

AI.tldr: Enhanced sensing of weak anharmonicities using a three-mode anti-PT symmetric cavity-magnon-waveguide system with optical gain control and detuned laser drive for improved sensitivity.
AI.motivation: To develop an enhanced sensing scheme for detecting weak nonlinearities (anharmonicities) in physical systems, particularly overcoming limitations when dissipative modes experience strong intrinsic decay.
AI.method: Proposes a three-mode anti-parity-time (anti-PT) symmetric cavity-magnon-waveguide system with optical gain applied to the active cavity mode, enabling flexible control of linewidth suppression points. Uses detuned laser drive to further improve sensitivity.
AI.result: Demonstrates high sensitivity for detecting weak nonlinearities in both cavity and magnonic modes, with sensitivity greatly improved using detuned laser drive. The scheme maintains effectiveness even when magnonic modes experience strong intrinsic decay.
AI.conclusion: The integrated passive-active three-mode anti-PT symmetric system provides a generalizable sensing scheme applicable to various physical systems with anharmonicities, offering enhanced detection capabilities through gain control and detuning optimization.

title: Structural coarse-graining enables noise-robust functional connectivity and reveals hidden inter-subject variability
summary: Functional connectivity estimates are highly sensitive to analysis choices and can be dominated by noise when the number of sampled time points is small relative to network dimensionality. This issue is particularly acute in fMRI, where scan resolution is limited. Because scan duration is constrained by practical factors (e.g., motion and fatigue), many datasets remain statistically underpowered for high-dimensional correlation estimation. We introduce a framework that combines diffusion-based structural coarse-graining with spectral noise filtering to recover statistically reliable functional networks from temporally limited data. The method reduces network dimensionality by grouping regions according to diffusion-defined communication. This produces coarse-grained networks with dimensions compatible with available time points, enabling random matrix filtering of noise-dominated modes. We benchmark three common FC pipelines against our approach. We find that raw-signal correlations are strongly influenced by non-stationary fluctuations that can reduce apparent inter-subject variability under limited sampling conditions. In contrast, our pipeline reveals a broader, multimodal landscape of inter-subject variability. These large-scale organization patterns are largely obscured by standard pipelines. Together, these results provide a practical route to reliable functional networks under realistic sampling constraints. This strategy helps separate noise-driven artifacts from reproducible patterns of human brain variability.

AI.tldr: A framework combining structural coarse-graining with spectral noise filtering to recover reliable functional networks from temporally limited fMRI data, revealing inter-subject variability patterns obscured by standard pipelines.
AI.motivation: Functional connectivity (FC) estimates in fMRI are highly sensitive to analysis choices and dominated by noise when sampled time points are limited relative to network dimensionality. Many datasets remain statistically underpowered for high-dimensional correlation estimation due to practical constraints on scan duration.
AI.method: Combines diffusion-based structural coarse-graining with spectral noise filtering. Reduces network dimensionality by grouping regions according to diffusion-defined communication, producing coarse-grained networks with dimensions compatible with available time points. Enables random matrix filtering of noise-dominated modes.
AI.result: Raw-signal correlations are strongly influenced by non-stationary fluctuations that reduce apparent inter-subject variability under limited sampling. The proposed pipeline reveals a broader, multimodal landscape of inter-subject variability. Large-scale organization patterns are largely obscured by standard pipelines.
AI.conclusion: Provides a practical route to reliable functional networks under realistic sampling constraints. Helps separate noise-driven artifacts from reproducible patterns of human brain variability.

title: Recursive QAOA for Interference-Aware Resource Allocation in Wireless Networks
summary: Discrete radio resource management problems in dense wireless networks are naturally cast as quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) programs but are difficult to solve at scale. We investigate a quantum-classical approach based on the Recursive Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (RQAOA), which interleaves shallow QAOA layers with variable elimination guided by measured single- and two-qubit correlators. For interference-aware channel assignment, we give a compact QUBO/Ising formulation in which pairwise interference induces same-channel couplings and one-hot constraints are enforced via quadratic penalties (or, optionally, constraint-preserving mixers). Within RQAOA, fixing high-confidence variables or relations reduces the problem dimension, stabilizes training, and concentrates measurement effort on a shrinking instance that is solved exactly once below a cutoff. On simulated instances of modest size, including a four-user, four-channel example, the method consistently returns feasible assignments and, for the demonstrated case, attains the global optimum. These results indicate that recursion can mitigate parameter growth and feasibility issues that affect plain QAOA, and suggest a viable pathway for near-term quantum heuristics in wireless resource allocation.

AI.tldr: RQAOA (Recursive Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm) applied to wireless channel assignment shows improved performance over plain QAOA by using variable elimination and recursion to handle feasibility constraints and scale better.
AI.motivation: Discrete radio resource management problems in dense wireless networks are naturally formulated as QUBO programs but are difficult to solve at scale. Quantum approaches like QAOA face parameter growth and feasibility issues, motivating the need for improved quantum-classical heuristics.
AI.method: Recursive Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (RQAOA) interleaves shallow QAOA layers with variable elimination guided by measured single- and two-qubit correlators. For interference-aware channel assignment, a compact QUBO/Ising formulation is used where pairwise interference induces same-channel couplings and one-hot constraints are enforced via quadratic penalties or constraint-preserving mixers.
AI.result: On simulated instances of modest size (including a four-user, four-channel example), the method consistently returns feasible assignments and attains the global optimum for the demonstrated case. RQAOA reduces problem dimension, stabilizes training, and concentrates measurement effort on shrinking instances.
AI.conclusion: Recursion can mitigate parameter growth and feasibility issues that affect plain QAOA, suggesting a viable pathway for near-term quantum heuristics in wireless resource allocation. RQAOA shows promise for practical quantum-classical approaches to discrete optimization problems in wireless networks.

title: Systematic Characterization of Transmon Qubit Stability with Thermal Cycling
summary: The temporal stability and reproducibility of qubit parameters are critical for the long-term operation and maintenance of superconducting quantum processors. In this work, we present a comprehensive longitudinal characterization of 27 frequency-tunable transmon qubits spanning over one year across four thermal cycles. Our results establish a distinct hierarchy of stability for superconducting hardware. We find that the intrinsic device parameters determining the qubit frequency and the baseline energy relaxation times ($T_1$) exhibit high robustness against thermal stress, characterized by frequency deviations typically confined within 0.5\% and non-degraded coherence baselines. In stark contrast, the environmental variables, specifically the background magnetic flux offsets and the microscopic landscape of two-level system (TLS) defects, undergo a significant stochastic reconfiguration after each cycle. By employing frequency-dependent relaxation spectroscopy and a quantitative metric, the $T_1$ Spectral Topography Fidelity, we demonstrate that thermal cycling acts as a ``hard reset'' for the local defect environment. This process introduces a level of spectral randomization equivalent to thousands of hours of continuous low-temperature evolution. These findings confirm that while the fabrication quality is preserved, the specific noise realization is statistically distinct for each thermal cycle, necessitating automated recalibration strategies for large-scale quantum systems.

AI.tldr: Thermal cycling acts as a "hard reset" for superconducting qubit environments, preserving intrinsic device parameters but randomizing flux offsets and TLS defects, requiring automated recalibration for quantum processors.
AI.motivation: To understand the long-term stability and reproducibility of superconducting qubit parameters, particularly how thermal cycling affects intrinsic device properties versus environmental variables, which is critical for reliable operation of quantum processors.
AI.method: Longitudinal characterization of 27 frequency-tunable transmon qubits over one year across four thermal cycles using frequency-dependent relaxation spectroscopy and T₁ Spectral Topography Fidelity metric.
AI.result: Intrinsic qubit parameters (frequency and baseline T₁) show high robustness (<0.5% frequency deviation, non-degraded coherence), while environmental variables (flux offsets and TLS defects) undergo significant stochastic reconfiguration after each thermal cycle, equivalent to thousands of hours of low-temperature evolution.
AI.conclusion: Thermal cycling preserves fabrication quality but randomizes the specific noise realization, necessitating automated recalibration strategies for large-scale quantum systems as each thermal cycle creates statistically distinct environmental configurations.

title: Squeezing-enhanced dual-channel interference for ground-state cooling of a levitated micromagnet with low quality factor
summary:
Cooling the center-of-mass (CM) motion of a macroscopic oscillator to its quantum ground state is a fundamental prerequisite for testing quantum mechanics at macroscopic scales. However, achieving this goal is currently hindered by the stringent requirement for an ultrahigh mechanical quality factor ($Q_c$). Here, we propose a dual-channel cooling scheme based on squeezing-enhanced quantum interference within a hybrid levitated cavity-magnomechanical system to overcome this limitation.
  By synergizing squeezing effects with quantum interference between the magnon-CM and cavity-CM channels, our scheme simultaneously suppresses Stokes (heating) scattering while enhancing anti-Stokes (cooling) scattering.~We demonstrate that this cooling mechanism reduces the critical $Q_c$ required for ground-state cooling by three orders of magnitude, making it achievable in the experimentally accessible regime of $Q_c \sim 10^4$. Furthermore, the net cooling rate is enhanced by nearly 180-fold compared to that of conventional single-channel cooling. This improvement is accompanied by a two orders of magnitude reduction in both the steady-state CM occupancy and the cooling time. Importantly, this enhanced performance remains robust even deep within the unresolved-sideband regime. Our results provide a feasible path toward preparing macroscopic quantum states by actively controlling the cooling dynamics, thereby relaxing the constraints on intrinsic material properties.

AI.tldr: Dual-channel cooling scheme using squeezing-enhanced quantum interference in a hybrid levitated cavity-magnomechanical system reduces mechanical quality factor requirement by 3 orders of magnitude for ground-state cooling.
AI.motivation: Achieving quantum ground state cooling of macroscopic oscillators is hindered by the stringent requirement for ultrahigh mechanical quality factors (Q_c). Current limitations prevent testing quantum mechanics at macroscopic scales.
AI.method: Proposes a dual-channel cooling scheme based on squeezing-enhanced quantum interference within a hybrid levitated cavity-magnomechanical system. Synergizes squeezing effects with quantum interference between magnon-CM and cavity-CM channels to simultaneously suppress Stokes (heating) scattering while enhancing anti-Stokes (cooling) scattering.
AI.result: The scheme reduces the critical Q_c required for ground-state cooling by three orders of magnitude (to Q_c ~ 10^4), enhances net cooling rate by nearly 180-fold compared to conventional single-channel cooling, reduces steady-state CM occupancy and cooling time by two orders of magnitude, and maintains robust performance even in unresolved-sideband regime.
AI.conclusion: Provides a feasible path toward preparing macroscopic quantum states by actively controlling cooling dynamics, relaxing constraints on intrinsic material properties and enabling ground-state cooling with experimentally accessible mechanical quality factors.

title: Characterization of Autofluorescence in Optical Fibers for NV-based Sensing Applications
summary: Optical fibers are crucial for guiding light in various sensing applications. Especially for quantum sensors such as the nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center in diamond, they enable light control and device miniaturization. However, fluorescence and scattering within the fiber, often referred to as fiber background, autofluorescence, or autoluminescence, can overlap spectrally with the NV centers' fluorescence, degrading the signal-to-noise ratio and thus limiting sensor sensitivity. Here, we investigate the optical spectra of standard optical fibers, considering material dependencies, physical influences, and their fluorescence scaling with excitation power and wavelength. Our results identify spectral components and fiber types with minimal unwanted background signals, guiding the selection of optimal fibers for NV-based quantum sensing.

AI.tldr: Analysis of optical fiber background fluorescence in NV-center quantum sensors, identifying optimal fiber types with minimal spectral interference.
AI.motivation: Optical fibers enable light control and miniaturization for quantum sensors like NV centers in diamond, but fiber background fluorescence (autofluorescence) spectrally overlaps with NV fluorescence, degrading signal-to-noise ratio and limiting sensor sensitivity.
AI.method: Investigation of optical spectra of standard optical fibers, analyzing material dependencies, physical influences, and fluorescence scaling with excitation power and wavelength.
AI.result: Identification of spectral components and specific fiber types with minimal unwanted background signals.
AI.conclusion: Provides guidance for selecting optimal fibers for NV-based quantum sensing by characterizing and minimizing fiber background interference.

title: BiBiEQ: Bivariate Bicycle Codes on Erasure Qubits
summary: Erasure qubits reduce overhead in fault-tolerant quantum error correction (QEC) by converting dominant faults into detectable errors known as erasures. They have demonstrated notable improvements in thresholds and scaling in surface and Floquet code memories. In this work, we use erasure qubits on Bivariate Bicycle (BB) codes from the quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) regime. Owing to their sparse structure and favorable rate-distance trade-offs, BB codes are practical candidates for QEC. We introduce BiBiEQ, a novel framework that compiles a given BB code into an erasure-aware memory circuit C_E. This erasure circuit C_E comprises erasure checks (ECs), resets, and erasures spread over a user-specified erasure check schedule (2EC, 4EC). BiBiEQ converts this erasure circuit C_E into the stabilizer circuit C for general-purpose decoding. BiBiEQ provides two engines for this conversion, BiBiEQ-Exact and BiBiEQ-Approx. BiBiEQ-Exact preserves the joint-erasure correlations and serves as our accuracy benchmark, while BiBiEQ-Approx uses an independence approximation to accelerate large sweeps and expose accuracy-throughput trade-offs. Using BiBiEQ, we decode the stabilizer circuits to get a per-round logical error rate (LER) for the BB codes and quantify the effect of the EC schedules on the correctable operating region below the pseudo-threshold. The 4EC schedule keeps the accuracy of both engines close to one another, making BiBiEQ-Approx a reliable proxy for BiBiEQ-Exact for faster sweeps. Below the pseudo-threshold, the code distance (d) hop from distance (d) 6 to 10 yields a drop in LER by 10-17x larger than distance (d) 10 to 12, showing that most gains are realized by d=10.

AI.tldr: BiBiEQ framework converts Bivariate Bicycle codes into erasure-aware memory circuits, enabling efficient fault-tolerant quantum error correction with erasure qubits through exact and approximate conversion engines.
AI.motivation: Erasure qubits reduce overhead in fault-tolerant quantum error correction by converting dominant faults into detectable erasures, but existing work has focused on surface and Floquet codes. This paper extends erasure qubit benefits to Bivariate Bicycle codes from the QLDPC regime, which offer practical advantages due to sparse structure and favorable rate-distance trade-offs.
AI.method: Introduces BiBiEQ framework that compiles BB codes into erasure-aware memory circuits (C_E) with erasure checks, resets, and erasures spread over user-specified schedules (2EC, 4EC). Provides two conversion engines: BiBiEQ-Exact (preserves joint-erasure correlations for accuracy benchmark) and BiBiEQ-Approx (uses independence approximation for faster sweeps). Converts erasure circuits to stabilizer circuits for general-purpose decoding.
AI.result: BiBiEQ decodes stabilizer circuits to obtain per-round logical error rates for BB codes, quantifying EC schedule effects on correctable operating region below pseudo-threshold. 4EC schedule keeps both engines' accuracy close, making BiBiEQ-Approx a reliable proxy for faster sweeps. Code distance hop from d=6 to 10 yields 10-17x larger LER drop than d=10 to 12, showing most gains realized by d=10.
AI.conclusion: BiBiEQ successfully extends erasure qubit advantages to Bivariate Bicycle codes, providing practical framework for QEC with erasure qubits in QLDPC regime. The 4EC schedule enables efficient approximation while maintaining accuracy, and distance scaling analysis reveals diminishing returns beyond d=10 for the studied codes.

title: Hidden Kinematics and Dual Quantum References in Magnetic Resonance
summary: Spin resonance phenomena are conventionally described using transition probabilities formulated in a rotating frame, whose physical meaning implicitly depends on the choice of quantum reference standard. In this Colloquium, we show that a spin in a rotating magnetic field constitutes a configuration involving two quantum descriptions that share a common quantization operator but differ in their kinematic and dynamical roles. The transition probability therefore emerges as a relational quantity between quantum reference standards rather than an intrinsic property of a single evolving spin state. By incorporating the kinematic motion of the spin vector together with the dynamical evolution, this framework restores consistent energy accounting and reveals the dual-reference structure underlying spin dynamics in rotating magnetic fields.

AI.tldr: Spin resonance in rotating magnetic fields reveals transition probabilities as relational quantities between quantum reference standards, not intrinsic properties of a single spin state.
AI.motivation: Conventional descriptions of spin resonance use transition probabilities in rotating frames, but these descriptions implicitly depend on quantum reference standard choices, creating ambiguity about the physical meaning of these probabilities.
AI.method: Analyze a spin in a rotating magnetic field as a configuration with two quantum descriptions sharing a common quantization operator but differing in kinematic and dynamical roles. Incorporate both kinematic motion of the spin vector and dynamical evolution to reveal the dual-reference structure.
AI.result: Transition probabilities emerge as relational quantities between quantum reference standards rather than intrinsic properties of a single evolving spin state. This framework restores consistent energy accounting in spin dynamics.
AI.conclusion: Spin dynamics in rotating magnetic fields has an underlying dual-reference structure where transition probabilities are fundamentally relational between quantum reference standards, providing a more consistent physical interpretation of spin resonance phenomena.

title: Two-phase driving of a linear radio-frequency ion trap
summary: A linear radio-frequency Paul trap is traditionally driven with one diagonal pair of electrodes grounded and the other connected to a high-voltage radio-frequency source. This method simplifies impedance matching of the voltage source to the trap. However, for several architectures it leads to increasing the axial micromotion amplitude, for example, when the capacitance between radio-frequency and end-cap electrodes is not negligible. Here, we present a technique to generate two high-voltage radio-frequency signals \SI{180}{\degree} out of phase to drive a linear Paul trap with opposite voltages between neighbouring electrodes. Using this, we have successfully trapped and cooled a chain of Ytterbium ions in a linear radio-frequency Paul trap.

AI.tldr: A technique for generating two 180° out-of-phase RF signals to drive linear Paul traps, reducing axial micromotion when capacitance between RF and end-cap electrodes is significant.
AI.motivation: Traditional linear RF Paul traps use one diagonal pair grounded and the other connected to RF source, which simplifies impedance matching but increases axial micromotion amplitude when capacitance between RF and end-cap electrodes is not negligible.
AI.method: Developed a technique to generate two high-voltage RF signals 180° out of phase to drive a linear Paul trap with opposite voltages between neighboring electrodes.
AI.result: Successfully trapped and cooled a chain of Ytterbium ions in a linear radio-frequency Paul trap using the new driving technique.
AI.conclusion: The phase-opposed RF driving technique provides an effective solution for reducing axial micromotion in linear Paul traps where traditional single-ended driving causes issues due to capacitive coupling.

title: Quantum Steering and Entanglement in a Tritter: Hierarchy under Loss
summary: Multipartite entangled states of continuous variables are fundamental resources for scalable quantum information processing. We study the correlation hierarchy in a tripartite state engineered by mixing a two-mode squeezed vacuum with a coherent state on a tritter, a key linear optical element for multimode state generation. Using the covariance matrix formalism, we comprehensively analyze the entanglement and Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen (EPR) steering among the output modes. The strength of both correlations is governed solely by the squeezing parameter and is independent of the coherent amplitude. We further examine the impact of inevitable optical losses in various channel configurations. The results show that while losses degrade correlations, EPR steering remains monogamous and exhibits stricter resilience thresholds than entanglement. Our analysis, supported by parameter extension techniques, confirms that the steering condition is more stringent than the inseparability criterion, clearly demonstrating that steering forms a strict subset of entanglement. These results elucidate the correlation structure in a readily generated multimode state and offer practical insights for developing asymmetric quantum protocols, such as one-sided device-independent tasks, where EPR steering serves as a critical resource.

AI.tldr: Tripartite CV states generated via mixing two-mode squeezed vacuum with coherent state on tritter; entanglement and EPR steering analyzed via covariance matrix, showing both depend only on squeezing parameter, with steering being stricter subset of entanglement that maintains monogamy under losses.
AI.motivation: To understand correlation hierarchy in multipartite continuous-variable states for scalable quantum information processing, particularly focusing on entanglement and EPR steering in tripartite states generated via linear optics, and their resilience to optical losses for practical asymmetric quantum protocols.
AI.method: Engineering tripartite state by mixing two-mode squeezed vacuum with coherent state on a tritter; using covariance matrix formalism to analyze entanglement and EPR steering among output modes; examining impact of optical losses in various channel configurations; employing parameter extension techniques to confirm steering conditions.
AI.result: Both entanglement and EPR steering strengths governed solely by squeezing parameter, independent of coherent amplitude; losses degrade correlations but EPR steering remains monogamous and exhibits stricter resilience thresholds than entanglement; steering condition is more stringent than inseparability criterion, confirming steering forms strict subset of entanglement.
AI.conclusion: The analysis elucidates correlation structure in readily generated multimode states and offers practical insights for developing asymmetric quantum protocols like one-sided device-independent tasks, where EPR steering serves as critical resource due to its stricter requirements and resilience properties.

title: Geometric criticality in the driven Jaynes-Cummings model
summary: When the photonic mode in the Jaynes-Cummings model is driven by an external classical field, the system can undergo the photon-blockade breakdown phase transition at a critical point. Such a phase transition has been detailedly investigated, but the critical properties of the eigenstates remain largely unexplored so far. We here study the geometric criticality associated with these eigenstates. The amplitude and phase of the drive serve as the control parameter of the governing Hamiltonian. We find the quantum metric and Berry curvature tensors for each eigenstate display divergent behaviors in the critical region. More importantly, the divergence associated with bright eigenstates is much more pronounced than that for the unique dark state. Our theoretical results can be experimentally confirmed in circuit quantum electrodynamics systems, where the driven Jaynes-Cummings model has been realized.

AI.tldr: The paper studies geometric criticality (quantum metric and Berry curvature) of eigenstates in a driven Jaynes-Cummings model, finding divergent behaviors near the photon-blockade breakdown phase transition, with bright states showing stronger divergence than the dark state.
AI.motivation: While the photon-blockade breakdown phase transition in driven Jaynes-Cummings models has been investigated, the critical properties of eigenstates (particularly geometric criticality) remain unexplored.
AI.method: Analyze quantum metric and Berry curvature tensors for eigenstates of a driven Jaynes-Cummings Hamiltonian, with drive amplitude and phase as control parameters, focusing on critical behavior near the phase transition.
AI.result: Quantum metric and Berry curvature tensors for eigenstates display divergent behaviors in the critical region, with bright eigenstates showing much more pronounced divergence than the unique dark state.
AI.conclusion: Theoretical results on geometric criticality can be experimentally confirmed in circuit quantum electrodynamics systems where driven Jaynes-Cummings models have been realized.

title: Semi-device-independent certification of high-dimensional quantum channels
summary: Certifying high-dimensional quantum channels is essential for ensuring the reliability of quantum communication protocols. Existing certification schemes often rely on fully trusted internal devices, which is difficult to achieve in realistic scenarios. Here, we propose a semi-device-independent framework for certifying channel properties directly from observed statistics, assuming only that the system dimension is known. By explicitly incorporating the full set of structural constraints inherent to Choi states, our approach exploits the Choi-Jamiołkowski isomorphism for rigorous certification of quantum channels. The entanglement dimensionality of quantum channels is first certified by introducing a witness and numerically determining its Schmidt-number-dependent bounds. This certification method reproduces known analytical benchmarks and is applied to dephasing and depolarizing noise channels, thereby confirming its validity. To provide a more complete assessment of channel performance, the entanglement fidelity of quantum channels is also certified using a hierarchy of semidefinite programming relaxations based on localizing matrices. Lower bounds on the entanglement fidelity are obtained that are compatible with either the full set of observed statistics or a single witness value.

AI.tldr: A semi-device-independent framework for certifying quantum channel properties using Choi-Jamiołkowski isomorphism, with methods for certifying entanglement dimensionality and entanglement fidelity from observed statistics.
AI.motivation: Existing quantum channel certification schemes require fully trusted internal devices, which is unrealistic in practical scenarios. There's a need for certification methods that work with minimal trust assumptions while still providing rigorous guarantees.
AI.method: Proposes a semi-device-independent framework assuming only known system dimension. Uses Choi-Jamiołkowski isomorphism and structural constraints of Choi states. Two main methods: 1) Certifying entanglement dimensionality via Schmidt-number-dependent witness bounds, 2) Certifying entanglement fidelity using semidefinite programming relaxations based on localizing matrices.
AI.result: The method reproduces known analytical benchmarks and is validated on dephasing and depolarizing noise channels. Lower bounds on entanglement fidelity are obtained that work with either full observed statistics or single witness values.
AI.conclusion: The framework enables rigorous certification of quantum channel properties with minimal trust assumptions, providing practical tools for assessing channel performance in realistic quantum communication scenarios.

title: Geometry-Enabled Radiation from Structured Paraxial Electrons
summary: We present a microscopic calculation of spontaneous photon emission by twisted (paraxial) electrons propagating through inhomogeneous, axisymmetric magnetic fields. We construct exact electron states that incorporate transverse mode structure and wavefront curvature by combining the Foldy-Wouthuysen transformation with a geometric framework based on Lewis-Ermakov invariants and metaplectic transformations. We show that the evolution of such structured states corresponds to an open path in the space of quadratic forms, giving rise to a geometric contribution to the emission amplitude that cannot be eliminated by gauge choice or adiabatic arguments. The inverse radius of curvature of the electron wavefront emerges as an effective geometric field that enables radiation even in regions where the external magnetic field vanishes locally. This mechanism generalizes Landau-level radiation to nonasymptotic, structured electron states and establishes a direct connection between noncyclic geometric evolution and photon emission.

AI.tldr: Spontaneous photon emission from twisted electrons in axisymmetric magnetic fields arises from geometric evolution of structured electron states, with wavefront curvature acting as an effective geometric field enabling radiation even where magnetic field vanishes locally.
AI.motivation: To understand photon emission from structured (twisted) electron states in inhomogeneous magnetic fields beyond conventional Landau-level radiation, particularly exploring how geometric evolution contributes to emission processes that cannot be explained by standard adiabatic or gauge arguments.
AI.method: Combines Foldy-Wouthuysen transformation with geometric framework using Lewis-Ermakov invariants and metaplectic transformations to construct exact electron states incorporating transverse mode structure and wavefront curvature; analyzes evolution as open path in quadratic form space.
AI.result: Shows that evolution of structured electron states corresponds to open path in quadratic form space, producing geometric contribution to emission amplitude; wavefront curvature acts as effective geometric field enabling radiation even where external magnetic field vanishes locally; generalizes Landau-level radiation to nonasymptotic structured states.
AI.conclusion: Establishes direct connection between noncyclic geometric evolution and photon emission, revealing that geometric contributions from structured electron states enable radiation mechanisms beyond conventional magnetic field interactions, with wavefront curvature serving as an effective geometric field source.

title: Minimal nonintegrable models with three-site interactions
summary: A systematic understanding of integrability breaking in translationally invariant spin chains with genuine three-site interactions remains lacking. In this work, we introduce and classify minimal nonintegrable spin-$1/2$ Hamiltonians, defined as models that saturate injectivity while admitting no nontrivial local conserved charges beyond the Hamiltonian. We first rigorously establish the nonintegrability of the deformed Fredkin spin chain with periodic boundary conditions by mapping it to a nearest-neighbor composite-spin representation and excluding all admissible $3$-local conserved charges. Guided by its structure, we then construct five classes of spin-$1/2$ models with genuine three-site interactions. One class is integrable, while the remaining four contain exactly two interaction terms and constitute the minimal nonintegrable three-site models. Our results delineate a sharp boundary between integrability and nonintegrability beyond the nearest-neighbor paradigm.

AI.tldr: Classification of minimal nonintegrable spin-1/2 Hamiltonians with genuine three-site interactions, establishing sharp boundary between integrability and nonintegrability beyond nearest-neighbor models.
AI.motivation: Lack of systematic understanding of integrability breaking in translationally invariant spin chains with genuine three-site interactions, aiming to define and classify minimal nonintegrable models.
AI.method: Rigorous establishment of nonintegrability of deformed Fredkin spin chain via mapping to nearest-neighbor composite-spin representation and exclusion of all admissible 3-local conserved charges; construction of five classes of spin-1/2 models with genuine three-site interactions.
AI.result: One class is integrable, while four classes with exactly two interaction terms constitute minimal nonintegrable three-site models, delineating sharp boundary between integrability and nonintegrability.
AI.conclusion: The work provides systematic classification of minimal nonintegrable spin-1/2 Hamiltonians with three-site interactions, establishing clear boundary between integrable and nonintegrable regimes beyond nearest-neighbor paradigm.

title: Quantum Evolution of Hopf Algebra Hamiltonians
summary: In recent years, growing attention has been devoted to the possibility that theories with deformed symmetries, associated with certain models of non-commutative spacetime, may encode a fundamental form of decoherence. This effect should be described by a Lindblad-like evolution governed by the non-trivial Hopf algebra structure of the time-evolution generators. In this work we provide a detailed analysis of such possibility for similar Hopf algebra deformations of the Hamiltonian of a qubit. Starting from a critical examination of the very definition of time evolution through the generalized adjoint action, we explore whether a coherent and physically viable framework can be established. In particular, our analysis shows that a more general combination of adjoint actions always guarantees a von Neumann dynamics and, also in the case of deformed spacetime symmetries considered in the literature, a physically viable Lindblad evolution cannot be established.

AI.tldr: The paper examines whether deformed spacetime symmetries (non-commutative geometry/Hopf algebra deformations) can produce fundamental decoherence via Lindblad-like evolution, focusing on qubit systems, and finds such physically viable evolution cannot be established.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether theories with deformed spacetime symmetries (non-commutative geometry models) can encode fundamental decoherence through Lindblad-like evolution governed by Hopf algebra structures, particularly examining qubit systems.
AI.method: Critical examination of time evolution definition via generalized adjoint action; analysis of Hopf algebra deformations of qubit Hamiltonians; exploration of whether coherent framework can be established using more general combinations of adjoint actions.
AI.result: A more general combination of adjoint actions always guarantees von Neumann dynamics, but physically viable Lindblad evolution cannot be established even for deformed spacetime symmetries considered in literature.
AI.conclusion: Despite theoretical interest in deformed symmetries encoding fundamental decoherence, the analysis shows that establishing physically viable Lindblad evolution from such Hopf algebra deformations is not possible, even with generalized adjoint action approaches.

title: Doubling the size of quantum selected configuration interaction based on seniority-zero space and its application to QC-QSCI-AFQMC
summary: We propose doubly occupied configuration interaction-quantum selected configuration interaction (DOCI-QSCI), which samples from the seniority-zero space. While the use of this space effectively doubles the qubit budget, equaling the number of spatial orbitals, this sector restriction can compromise quantitative accuracy. To compensate for this, we expand sampled bitstrings via their Cartesian product into a larger space that includes seniority-breaking determinants. The resulting wave function is also proposed using the trial state in phaseless auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (ph-AFQMC) to recover dynamical correlations across the full orbital space (DOCI-QSCI-AFQMC). We evaluate the proposed methods on the H6 chain, N2 dissociation, and the addition of singlet O2 to a BODIPY dye. For the H6 chain, DOCI-QSCI-AFQMC reproduces the accuracy of the level of the complete-active-space counterpart with the quantum device ibm kobe. For N2 and BODIPY-O2, with (14e, 28o) and up to (20e, 20o) active spaces, it yields reasonable results, whereas single-reference CCSD(T) fails qualitatively. These results demonstrate that the DOCI-QSCI doubles the orbital space accessible to conventional QSCI and subsequent ph-AFQMC post-processing delivers reasonably high accuracy.

AI.tldr: DOCI-QSCI method samples seniority-zero space, doubles qubit budget, and uses ph-AFQMC post-processing to recover dynamical correlations, achieving high accuracy for challenging systems where CCSD(T) fails.
AI.motivation: To overcome limitations of conventional QSCI by expanding accessible orbital space while maintaining quantum computational efficiency, and to address cases where single-reference methods like CCSD(T) fail qualitatively for strongly correlated systems.
AI.method: DOCI-QSCI samples from seniority-zero space (doubles qubit budget to equal number of spatial orbitals), expands sampled bitstrings via Cartesian product into seniority-breaking determinants, and uses the resulting wave function as trial state in ph-AFQMC to recover dynamical correlations across full orbital space.
AI.result: For H6 chain, DOCI-QSCI-AFQMC reproduces accuracy of complete-active-space counterpart using quantum device ibm kobe. For N2 (14e, 28o) and BODIPY-O2 (up to 20e, 20o) active spaces, yields reasonable results where CCSD(T) fails qualitatively. Doubles orbital space accessible to conventional QSCI.
AI.conclusion: DOCI-QSCI effectively doubles orbital space accessible to conventional QSCI, and subsequent ph-AFQMC post-processing delivers reasonably high accuracy for challenging strongly correlated systems, demonstrating a promising hybrid quantum-classical approach.

title: Real-Time Magnetic Field Sensing based on Microwave Frequency Modulated Photocurrent of Nitrogen-Vacancy Centers in Diamond
summary: While photoelectric detection of magnetic resonance (PDMR) can be applied to miniaturize nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center-based quantum sensors, the real demonstration of PDMR-based magnetic field sensing remains as a distinctive challenge. To tackle this challenge, in this article, we fabricate diamond samples with electrodes and microwave antenna on the surface, and realize PDMR by detecting photocurrent in nanoampere range via various lock-in amplifying modes. Importantly, we obtain a theoretical and experimental sensitivity 397 nT/Hz and 921 nT/Hz of magnetic field detection in DC-10 Hz range with a laser intensity and microwave frequency modulated mode, respectively, and demonstrate for the first time, a real-time tracking of alternating magnetic field with a standard deviation of 1.5 uT. Furthermore, we investigate systematically the dependence of the PDMR contrast, linewidth and the sensitivity on the laser and microwave power, and find a perfect agreement with a master equation based theoretical model, which accounts for not only the optically induced charge switch of neutral and negative NV centers, but also the interaction with microwave field.

AI.tldr: First demonstration of real-time magnetic field sensing using photoelectric detection of magnetic resonance (PDMR) with NV centers, achieving sensitivities of 397-921 nT/√Hz and tracking alternating fields with 1.5 μT precision.
AI.motivation: PDMR can miniaturize NV-based quantum sensors, but real demonstration of PDMR-based magnetic field sensing remains a distinctive challenge that needs to be addressed.
AI.method: Fabricated diamond samples with electrodes and microwave antenna on surface, realized PDMR by detecting nanoampere-range photocurrent via various lock-in amplifying modes, including laser intensity and microwave frequency modulated modes.
AI.result: Achieved theoretical sensitivity 397 nT/√Hz and experimental sensitivity 921 nT/√Hz in DC-10 Hz range, demonstrated first real-time tracking of alternating magnetic field with 1.5 μT standard deviation, and found perfect agreement between experimental PDMR parameters and master equation model.
AI.conclusion: Successfully demonstrated PDMR-based magnetic field sensing for the first time, validated theoretical model accounting for NV charge switching and microwave interactions, enabling miniaturized quantum sensors with practical sensing capabilities.

title: Full Schmidt characterization of spatiotemporally entangled states produced from spontaneous parametric down-conversion
summary: The full Schmidt decomposition of spatiotemporally entangled states generated from spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) has not been carried out until now due to the immense computational complexity arising from the large dimensionalities of the states. In this Letter, we utilize the rotational symmetry of the states to reduce the complexity by at least four orders of magnitude and carry out the decomposition to reveal the precise forms of the spatiotemporal Schmidt modes and the Schmidt spectrum spanning over 10^4 modes. We show that the Schmidt modes have a phase profile with a transverse spatial vortex structure that endows them with orbital angular momentum at all frequencies. In the high-gain regime, these Schmidt modes broaden and the Schmidt spectrum narrows with increasing pump strength. Our work can spur novel applications at the intersection of quantum imaging and spectroscopy that utilize entangled states produced from SPDC.

AI.tldr: Researchers perform the first full Schmidt decomposition of spatiotemporally entangled states from SPDC by exploiting rotational symmetry to reduce computational complexity by 4+ orders of magnitude, revealing vortex-structured Schmidt modes with orbital angular momentum across frequencies.
AI.motivation: The full Schmidt decomposition of spatiotemporally entangled states generated from spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) has not been achieved previously due to immense computational complexity from the large dimensionalities of these states.
AI.method: Utilize the rotational symmetry of the SPDC states to reduce computational complexity by at least four orders of magnitude, enabling the complete Schmidt decomposition to reveal precise forms of spatiotemporal Schmidt modes and Schmidt spectrum spanning over 10^4 modes.
AI.result: The Schmidt modes exhibit a phase profile with transverse spatial vortex structure that endows them with orbital angular momentum at all frequencies. In the high-gain regime, these Schmidt modes broaden and the Schmidt spectrum narrows with increasing pump strength.
AI.conclusion: This work enables novel applications at the intersection of quantum imaging and spectroscopy that utilize entangled states produced from SPDC by providing the first complete characterization of their spatiotemporal Schmidt decomposition.

title: Higher-Order Corrections to Scrambling Dynamics in Brownian Spin SYK Models
summary: We investigate operator growth in a Brownian spin Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev (SYK) model with random all-to-all interactions, focusing on the full operator-size distribution. For Hamiltonians containing interactions of order two up to $L$, we derive a closed master equation for the Pauli-string expansion coefficients and recast their dynamics into a generating-function formulation suitable for the large-$N$ limit. This approach allows us to diagonalize the leading-order evolution operator explicitly and obtain exact solutions for arbitrary initial operator distributions, including the effects of decoherence. Going beyond leading order, we develop a systematic $1/N$ expansion that captures higher-order corrections to the operator-size dynamics and the late-time behavior. Our results demonstrate that higher-order effects play a crucial role in operator scrambling and that the full operator-size distribution provides a more refined probe of quantum chaos in Brownian and open quantum systems.

AI.tldr: Exact solution of operator-size dynamics in Brownian SYK models with systematic 1/N expansion reveals crucial higher-order effects in quantum chaos.
AI.motivation: To understand operator growth and scrambling in Brownian SYK models, particularly focusing on the full operator-size distribution beyond leading order approximations, and to study the effects of decoherence on quantum chaos.
AI.method: Derived closed master equation for Pauli-string expansion coefficients, developed generating-function formulation for large-N limit, diagonalized leading-order evolution operator, and established systematic 1/N expansion for higher-order corrections to operator-size dynamics.
AI.result: Obtained exact solutions for arbitrary initial operator distributions including decoherence effects, demonstrated crucial role of higher-order effects in operator scrambling, and showed that full operator-size distribution provides refined probe of quantum chaos in Brownian and open systems.
AI.conclusion: Higher-order corrections are essential for understanding operator scrambling dynamics, and the complete operator-size distribution offers a more detailed characterization of quantum chaos than simpler measures, particularly in Brownian and open quantum systems.

title: Quantum self-interaction within an infinitely deep cavity
summary: One examines the infinitely deep quantum cavity, also known as the quantum infinite square well, within the framework of the real Hilbert space. The solutions are considered in terms of complex wave functions, and also in terms of quaternionic wave functions. The complex results reproduce the usual achievements established in the complex Hilbert space, but also extend them to non-stationary solutions, as well as to distorted stationary solutions, different energy spectra, and dislocated observed position. The quaternionic cases further admit the incidence of self-interaction, something that cannot be observed in complex solutions. Therefore, both the complex and quaternionic solutions are more general than previous cases, thus opening the way to further one-dimensional solutions to be researched in the non-relativistic theory.

AI.tldr: Analysis of quantum infinite square well in real Hilbert space using complex and quaternionic wave functions, revealing extended solutions beyond conventional complex Hilbert space results.
AI.motivation: To explore quantum mechanics in a real Hilbert space framework and investigate how complex and quaternionic wave functions extend beyond conventional complex Hilbert space solutions for the infinite square well problem.
AI.method: Examination of the infinitely deep quantum cavity (quantum infinite square well) within real Hilbert space framework, analyzing solutions using both complex and quaternionic wave functions, comparing results with conventional complex Hilbert space solutions.
AI.result: Complex solutions reproduce conventional results but also extend to non-stationary solutions, distorted stationary solutions, different energy spectra, and dislocated observed positions. Quaternionic cases additionally admit self-interaction phenomena not observable in complex solutions.
AI.conclusion: Both complex and quaternionic solutions in real Hilbert space are more general than previous cases, opening new avenues for one-dimensional solutions in non-relativistic quantum theory.

title: Improved entanglement-based high-dimensional optical quantum computation with linear optics
summary: Quantum gates are the essential block for quantum computer. High-dimensional quantum gates exhibit remarkable advantages over their two-dimensional counterparts for some quantum information processing tasks. Here we present a family of entanglement-based optical controlled-SWAP gates on $\mathbb{C}^{2}\otimes \mathbb{C}^{d}\otimes \mathbb{C}^{d}$. With the hybrid encoding, we encode the control qubits and target qudits in photonic polarization and spatial degrees of freedom, respectively. The circuit is constructed using only $(2+3d)$ ($d\geq 2$) linear optics, beating an earlier result of 14 linear optics with $d=2$. The circuit depth 5 is much lower than an earlier result of 11 with $d=2$. Besides, the fidelity of the presented circuit can reach 99.4\%, and it is higher than the previous counterpart with $d=2$. Our scheme are constructed in a deterministic way without any borrowed ancillary photons or measurement-induced nonlinearities. Moreover, our approach allows $d>2$.

AI.tldr: A family of entanglement-based optical controlled-SWAP gates for high-dimensional quantum systems (C²⊗Cᵈ⊗Cᵈ) using hybrid encoding with only (2+3d) linear optics, achieving circuit depth 5 and 99.4% fidelity deterministically without ancillary photons.
AI.motivation: High-dimensional quantum gates offer advantages over two-dimensional counterparts for quantum information processing, but existing implementations require many optical components (14 for d=2) and have high circuit depth (11 for d=2). There's a need for more efficient, high-fidelity implementations that scale better with dimension.
AI.method: Hybrid encoding: control qubits encoded in photonic polarization degrees of freedom, target qudits encoded in spatial degrees of freedom. Circuit constructed using only (2+3d) linear optical elements (d≥2). The approach is deterministic, requiring no borrowed ancillary photons or measurement-induced nonlinearities.
AI.result: For d=2: uses only 8 linear optics (vs. previous 14), circuit depth 5 (vs. previous 11), fidelity reaches 99.4% (higher than previous). The scheme scales to d>2 with (2+3d) components, maintaining deterministic operation without ancillary resources.
AI.conclusion: The presented family of controlled-SWAP gates provides a more resource-efficient, higher-fidelity implementation for high-dimensional quantum systems, with better scaling properties and deterministic operation, advancing practical high-dimensional quantum information processing.

title: An efficient method for spot-checking quantum properties with sequential trials
summary: In practical situations, the reliability of quantum resources can be compromised due to complex generation processes or adversarial manipulations during transmission. Consequently, the trials generated sequentially in an experiment may exhibit non-independent and non-identically distributed (non-i.i.d.) behavior. This non-i.i.d. behavior can introduce security concerns and result in faulty estimates when performing information tasks such as quantum key distribution, self-testing, verifiable quantum computation, and resource allocation in quantum networks. To certify the performance of such tasks, one can make a random decision in each trial, either spot-checking some desired property or utilizing the quantum resource for the given task. However, a general method for certification with a sequence of non-i.i.d. spot-checking trials is still missing. Here, we develop such a method. This method not only works efficiently with a finite number of trials but also yields asymptotically tight certificates of performance. Our analysis shows that even as the total number of trials approaches infinity, only a constant number of trials needs to be spot-checked on average to certify the average performance of the remaining trials at a specified confidence level.

AI.tldr: A general certification method for quantum information tasks using spot-checking trials that works with non-i.i.d. sequences, requiring only constant spot-checking overhead even as total trials approach infinity.
AI.motivation: Quantum resources in practical scenarios often exhibit non-i.i.d. behavior due to complex generation processes or adversarial manipulations, compromising reliability and introducing security concerns in quantum key distribution, self-testing, verifiable quantum computation, and quantum network resource allocation. Existing methods lack general certification approaches for non-i.i.d. spot-checking trials.
AI.method: Developed a general certification method using random spot-checking decisions in each trial, where some trials are used to check desired properties while others utilize the quantum resource. The method handles non-i.i.d. sequences efficiently with finite trials and provides asymptotically tight performance certificates.
AI.result: The method demonstrates that even as total trials approach infinity, only a constant number of trials needs to be spot-checked on average to certify the average performance of remaining trials at specified confidence levels. The approach provides efficient finite-trial analysis and asymptotically optimal certification.
AI.conclusion: The developed certification method addresses the critical need for reliable performance verification in quantum information tasks under realistic non-i.i.d. conditions, offering practical and efficient certification with minimal spot-checking overhead while maintaining rigorous security guarantees.

title: Optimal Quantum Speedups for Repeatedly Nested Expectation Estimation
summary: We study the estimation of repeatedly nested expectations (RNEs) with a constant horizon (number of nestings) using quantum computing. We propose a quantum algorithm that achieves $\varepsilon$-error with cost $\tilde O(\varepsilon^{-1})$, up to logarithmic factors. Standard lower bounds show this scaling is essentially optimal, yielding an almost quadratic speedup over the best classical algorithm. Our results extend prior quantum speedups for single nested expectations to repeated nesting, and therefore cover a broader range of applications, including optimal stopping. This extension requires a new derandomized variant of the classical randomized Multilevel Monte Carlo (rMLMC) algorithm. Careful de-randomization is key to overcoming a variable-time issue that typically increases quantized versions of classical randomized algorithms.

AI.tldr: Quantum algorithm achieves $\tilde O(\varepsilon^{-1})$ cost for estimating repeatedly nested expectations, providing almost quadratic speedup over classical methods.
AI.motivation: Extend quantum speedups from single nested expectations to repeated nesting (constant horizon) to cover broader applications including optimal stopping problems.
AI.method: Develop quantum algorithm using derandomized variant of classical randomized Multilevel Monte Carlo (rMLMC) to overcome variable-time issues in quantized versions of randomized algorithms.
AI.result: Achieves $\varepsilon$-error with cost $\tilde O(\varepsilon^{-1})$ (optimal scaling), providing almost quadratic speedup over best classical algorithm.
AI.conclusion: Successfully extends quantum advantages to repeatedly nested expectations, enabling faster estimation for applications like optimal stopping through careful derandomization techniques.

title: Spinor Double-Quantum Excitation in the Solution NMR of Near-Equivalent Spin-1/2 Pairs
summary: A family of double-quantum excitation schemes is described for the solution nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) of near-equivalent spin-1/2 pairs. These new methods exploit the spinor behaviour of 2-level systems, whose signature is the change of sign of a quantum state upon a $2π$ rotation. The spinor behaviour is used to manipulate the phases of single-quantum coherences, in order to prepare a double-quantum precursor state which is rapidly converted into double-quantum coherence by a straightforward $π/2$ rotation. One set of spinor-based methods exploits symmetry-based pulse sequences, while the other set exploits SLIC (spin-lock-induced crossing), in which the nutation frequency under a resonant radiofrequency field is matched to the spin-spin coupling. A variant of SLIC is introduced which is well-compensated for deviations in the radiofrequency field amplitude. The methods are demonstrated by performing double-quantum-filtered $^{19}$F NMR on a molecular system containing a pair of diastereotopic $^{19}$F nuclei. The new methods are compared with existing techniques.

AI.tldr: Novel NMR double-quantum excitation schemes exploiting spinor behavior for near-equivalent spin-1/2 pairs, demonstrated with 19F NMR on diastereotopic nuclei.
AI.motivation: To develop improved methods for exciting double-quantum coherence in near-equivalent spin-1/2 pairs in solution NMR, addressing limitations of existing techniques.
AI.method: Two approaches: 1) symmetry-based pulse sequences exploiting spinor behavior to manipulate single-quantum coherence phases, and 2) SLIC (spin-lock-induced crossing) methods with RF field amplitude matching spin-spin coupling, including a robust variant compensating for RF field deviations.
AI.result: Successfully demonstrated through double-quantum-filtered 19F NMR on a molecular system containing diastereotopic 19F nuclei, showing effective excitation of double-quantum coherence in near-equivalent spin pairs.
AI.conclusion: Spinor-based excitation schemes provide effective new tools for double-quantum NMR of near-equivalent spin-1/2 pairs, with both symmetry-based and SLIC approaches offering advantages over existing methods.

title: Detecting multilevel entanglement from light-based entanglement witnesses
summary: We introduce a set of electric-field based inequalities capable of detecting multilevel entanglement from a system of N quantum emitters. We determine that the polarization channel as well as the direction of detection can enhance entanglement detection, a feature specific to multilevel systems. We demonstrate the efficiency of the witnesses to detect genuine multipartite entanglement by applying it to families of paradigmatic quantum states, such as Dicke states, singlet states and W-like states. The detection is not only robust to noise, but also applies to mixed entangled states. Our findings open up possibilities for the detection of entanglement without local measurements in systems of multilevel emitters such as superconducting qubits, Rydberg atoms or quantum dots.

AI.tldr: Electric-field based inequalities detect multilevel entanglement in N quantum emitters without local measurements, with polarization and detection direction enhancing detection for multilevel systems.
AI.motivation: To develop entanglement detection methods for multilevel quantum systems that don't require local measurements, addressing the need for practical entanglement verification in complex quantum systems like superconducting qubits, Rydberg atoms, and quantum dots.
