AI.method: Introduce electric-field based inequalities that leverage polarization channels and detection directions to detect multilevel entanglement. The method is applied to paradigmatic quantum states including Dicke states, singlet states, and W-like states.
AI.result: The witnesses efficiently detect genuine multipartite entanglement, are robust to noise, work for mixed entangled states, and show enhanced detection capabilities through polarization channels and detection direction optimization specific to multilevel systems.
AI.conclusion: The approach enables entanglement detection without local measurements in multilevel emitter systems, opening new possibilities for practical entanglement verification in various quantum platforms.

title: Preparing squeezed, cat and GKP states with parity measurements
summary: Bosonic modes constitute a central resource in a wide range of quantum technologies, providing long-lived degrees of freedom for the storage, processing, and transduction of quantum information. Such modes naturally arise in platforms including circuit quantum electrodynamics, quantum acoustodynamics, and trapped-ion systems. In these architectures, coherent control and high-fidelity readout of the bosonic degrees of freedom are achieved via coupling to an auxiliary qubit. When operated in the strong dispersive regime, this interaction enables parity measurements of the mode which, in combination with phase-space displacements, constitute a standard experimental tool for full Wigner-function tomography. Here, we propose a protocol based on displaced parity measurements that allows for the preparation of a variety of bosonic quantum states. As a first example, we demonstrate the generation of squeezed states, achieving up to ~9 dB of squeezing after only three parity measurements, and show that the protocol is robust against experimental imperfections. Finally, we generalize our approach to the preparation of other paradigmatic bosonic states, including cat and Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill states.

AI.tldr: Protocol using displaced parity measurements to prepare various bosonic quantum states including squeezed, cat, and GKP states with high squeezing achieved in few measurements.
AI.motivation: Bosonic modes are crucial for quantum technologies but require efficient state preparation methods; existing approaches based on Wigner tomography need to be extended to state generation.
AI.method: Protocol based on displaced parity measurements in strong dispersive regime, using qubit-boson coupling for parity readout combined with phase-space displacements to iteratively prepare target states.
AI.result: Demonstrated generation of squeezed states achieving ~9 dB squeezing after only three parity measurements; protocol shown to be robust against experimental imperfections; generalized to cat and Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill states.
AI.conclusion: Displaced parity measurements provide efficient and robust method for preparing various bosonic quantum states, offering practical advantages for quantum information processing with bosonic modes.

title: The simplified quantum circuits for implementing quantum teleportation
summary: It is crucial to design quantum circuits as small as possible and as shallow as possible for quantum information processing tasks. We design quantum circuits with simplified gate-count, cost, and depth for implementing quantum teleportation among various entangled channels. Here the gate-count/cost/depth of the Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger-based quantum teleportation is reduced from 10/6/8 to 9/4/6, the two-qubit-cluster-based quantum teleportation is reduced from 9/4/5 to 6/3/5, the three-qubit-cluster-based quantum teleportation is reduced from 12/6/7 to 8/4/5, the Brown-based quantum teleportation is reduced from 25/15/17 to 18/8/7, the Borras-based quantum teleportation is reduced from 36/25/20 to 15/8/11, and the entanglement-swapping-based quantum teleportation is reduced from 13/8/8 to 10/5/5. Note that, no feed-forward recover operation is required in the simplified schemes. Moreover, the experimentally demonstrations on IBM quantum computer indicate that our simplified and compressed schemes can be realized with good fidelity.

AI.tldr: The paper presents optimized quantum circuits for teleportation across various entangled channels, achieving significant reductions in gate-count, cost, and depth while eliminating feed-forward recovery operations.
AI.motivation: Quantum circuits need to be as small and shallow as possible for efficient quantum information processing. Existing quantum teleportation implementations across different entangled channels have suboptimal circuit complexity metrics (gate-count, cost, depth) that can be improved.
AI.method: The authors design simplified quantum circuits for teleportation across six different entangled channels: GHZ, two-qubit cluster, three-qubit cluster, Brown, Borras, and entanglement-swapping states. They optimize circuits by reducing gate-count, cost, and depth while eliminating feed-forward recovery operations. Experimental validation is performed on IBM quantum computers.
AI.result: Significant reductions achieved: GHZ-based teleportation reduced from 10/6/8 to 9/4/6; two-qubit-cluster from 9/4/5 to 6/3/5; three-qubit-cluster from 12/6/7 to 8/4/5; Brown from 25/15/17 to 18/8/7; Borras from 36/25/20 to 15/8/11; entanglement-swapping from 13/8/8 to 10/5/5. No feed-forward recovery needed. Experimental demonstrations on IBM quantum computers show good fidelity.
AI.conclusion: The paper successfully demonstrates optimized quantum teleportation circuits with reduced complexity metrics across multiple entangled channels. The simplified schemes are experimentally feasible on current quantum hardware and eliminate the need for feed-forward operations, making them more practical for near-term quantum devices.

title: Quantum-classical framework for many-fermion response and structure
summary: Response functions are key observables for probing the structure and dynamics of many-body systems. We introduce and demonstrate a quantum-classical framework for computing response functions of general many-fermion systems that also provides the full bound-state spectrum. The framework employs the Lorentz integral transform and a new Hamiltonian input scheme that enables practical and scalable circuit constructions for general many-fermion Hamiltonians. Within this framework, we develop a hybrid strategy to evaluate the Lorentz integral and propose three protocols to extract response functions and bound-state structural information. As a demonstration, we apply the method to \({}^{19}\mathrm{O}\) with realistic internucleon interactions, computing both the bound-state spectrum and the response function. We envision that our approach will open new avenues for exploring the structure and dynamics of a broad class of many-body systems across diverse fields.

AI.tldr: Quantum-classical framework for computing response functions and bound-state spectra of many-fermion systems using Lorentz integral transform and scalable circuit constructions.
AI.motivation: Response functions are crucial observables for probing structure and dynamics of many-body systems, but computing them for general many-fermion systems remains challenging.
AI.method: Introduces quantum-classical framework using Lorentz integral transform with new Hamiltonian input scheme for practical/scalable circuit constructions, plus hybrid strategy for evaluating Lorentz integral and three protocols for extracting response functions and bound-state information.
AI.result: Method successfully applied to ¹⁹O with realistic internucleon interactions, computing both bound-state spectrum and response function.
AI.conclusion: The approach opens new avenues for exploring structure and dynamics of many-body systems across diverse fields.

title: Quantum Detection of Sequency-Band Structure
summary: We present a quantum algorithm for estimating the amplitude content of user-specified sequency bands in quantum-encoded signals. The method employs a sequency-ordered Quantum Walsh-Hadamard Transform (QWHT), a comparator-based oracle that coherently marks basis states within an arbitrary sequency range, and Quantum Amplitude Estimation (QAE) to estimate the total probability mass in the selected band. This enables the detection of structured signal components, including both high- and low-sequency features, as well as the identification of rapid sign-change behavior associated with noise or anomalies. The proposed method can be embedded as a module within a larger quantum algorithm; in this setting, both the input and output remain fully quantum, enabling seamless integration with upstream and downstream quantum operations. We show that the sequency-ordered QWHT can be implemented with circuit depth $O(\log_2 N)$ (equivalently $O(n)$ for $N=2^n$) when acting on an amplitude-encoded quantum state, whereas computing the full Walsh-Hadamard spectrum of an explicit length-$N$ classical signal requires $O(N\log_2 N)$ operations via the fast Walsh-Hadamard transform. This results in an exponential quantum advantage when the QWHT is used as a modular block within a larger quantum algorithm, relative to classical fast Walsh-Hadamard transform-based approaches operating on explicit data. From an application perspective, the proposed sequency band-energy estimation may be interpreted as a structure-based anomaly indicator, enabling the detection of unexpected high-sequency components relative to a nominal low-sequency signal class. The algorithm is applicable to quantum-enhanced signal processing tasks such as zero-crossing analysis, band-limited noise estimation, and feature extraction in the Walsh basis.

AI.tldr: Quantum algorithm for estimating amplitude content in specified sequency bands of quantum-encoded signals using QWHT, comparator oracle, and QAE, achieving exponential quantum advantage over classical approaches.
AI.motivation: Enable quantum-enhanced signal processing with efficient detection of structured signal components (both high- and low-sequency features) and identification of rapid sign-change behavior associated with noise or anomalies in quantum-encoded signals.
AI.method: Uses sequency-ordered Quantum Walsh-Hadamard Transform (QWHT) with O(log₂N) circuit depth, a comparator-based oracle to coherently mark basis states within arbitrary sequency range, and Quantum Amplitude Estimation (QAE) to estimate total probability mass in selected band.
AI.result: Achieves exponential quantum advantage when QWHT is used as modular block within larger quantum algorithm (O(log₂N) vs O(Nlog₂N) for classical fast Walsh-Hadamard transform), enabling structure-based anomaly detection and quantum-enhanced signal processing applications.
AI.conclusion: The algorithm provides efficient quantum signal processing for sequency band-energy estimation, serving as structure-based anomaly indicator and enabling seamless integration with upstream/downstream quantum operations in larger quantum algorithms.

title: Efficient circuit compression by multi-qudit entangling gates in linear optical quantum computation
summary: Linear optical quantum computation (LOQC) offers a promising platform for scalable quantum information processing, but its scalability is fundamentally constrained by the probabilistic nature of non-local entangling gates. Qudit circuit compression schemes mitigate this issue by encoding multiple qubits onto qudits. However, these schemes become inefficient when only a subset of the encoded qubits is required to participate in the non-local entangling gate, leading to an exponential increase in the number of non-local gates. In this Letter, we address this bottleneck by demonstrating the existence of multi-level control-Z (CZ) gates for qudits encoded in multiple spatial modes in LOQC. Unlike conventional two-level CZ gates, which act only on a single pair of modes, multi-level CZ gates impart a conditional phase shift for an arbitrarily chosen subset of the spatial modes. We present two explicit linear optical schemes that realize such operations, illustrating a fundamental trade-off between prior information about the input quantum state and the physical resources required. The first scheme is realized with a constant success probability of $1/8$ independent of the qudit dimension using a single non-local entangling gate, at the cost of state dependence, which is significantly better than the current success probability of $1/9$. Our second scheme provides a fully state independent realization reducing the number of non-local gates to $\mathcal{O}(2^{r_1}+2^{r_2})$ as compared to the existing bound of $\mathcal{O}(2^{r_1+r_2})$ where $r_1$ and $r_2$ are the number of qubits to be removed as control in the qudits. The success probability of the realization is $\frac{1}{2} \left(\frac{1}{8}\right)^{2^{r_1}+2^{r_2}}$. When combined with qudit circuit compression schemes, our results improve upon a key scalability limitation and significantly improve the efficiency of LOQC architectures.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces multi-level CZ gates for qudits in LOQC that can conditionally phase shift arbitrary subsets of spatial modes, overcoming scalability bottlenecks in qudit circuit compression schemes.
AI.motivation: LOQC scalability is constrained by probabilistic non-local entangling gates. Qudit circuit compression schemes become inefficient when only a subset of encoded qubits needs non-local gates, causing exponential growth in gate count.
AI.method: Two linear optical schemes for multi-level CZ gates: (1) constant success probability 1/8 scheme using single non-local gate (state-dependent), (2) state-independent scheme reducing non-local gates from O(2^{r1+r2}) to O(2^{r1}+2^{r2}).
AI.result: First scheme achieves 1/8 success probability (improving on current 1/9) with single non-local gate. Second scheme provides state-independent realization with exponential reduction in non-local gate count.
AI.conclusion: Multi-level CZ gates combined with qudit circuit compression significantly improve LOQC scalability and efficiency by addressing key bottlenecks in non-local gate requirements.

title: The Finite Geometry of Breaking Quantum Secrets
summary: Using a finite geometric framework for studying the pentagon and heptagon codes we show that the concepts of quantum secret sharing and contextuality can be studied in a nice and unified manner. The basic idea is a careful study of the respective $2+3$ and $3+4$ tensorial factorizations of the elements of the stabilizer groups of these codes. It is demonstrated in detail how finite geometric structures entailing a specific three-qubit (resp. four-qubit) embedding of binary symplectic polar spaces of rank two (resp. three), corresponding to these factorizations, govern issues of contextuality and entanglement needed for a geometric understanding of quantum secret sharing. Using these results for the $(3,5)$ and $(4,7)$ threshold schemes explicit secret breaking protocols are derived. Our results hint at a novel geometric way of looking at contextual configurations.

AI.tldr: The paper shows how finite geometry unifies quantum secret sharing and contextuality via pentagon/heptagon codes, using tensor factorizations to reveal geometric structures governing entanglement and contextuality, with explicit secret-breaking protocols for threshold schemes.
AI.motivation: To establish a unified geometric framework connecting quantum secret sharing and contextuality through finite geometric structures, demonstrating how specific tensor factorizations reveal underlying geometric patterns that govern both phenomena.
AI.method: Using finite geometric framework to study pentagon and heptagon codes; analyzing 2+3 and 3+4 tensorial factorizations of stabilizer group elements; embedding binary symplectic polar spaces into three-qubit and four-qubit systems; deriving explicit secret breaking protocols for (3,5) and (4,7) threshold schemes.
AI.result: Demonstrated how finite geometric structures govern contextuality and entanglement for quantum secret sharing; derived explicit secret breaking protocols for threshold schemes; revealed novel geometric perspective on contextual configurations through specific qubit embeddings of binary symplectic polar spaces.
AI.conclusion: Finite geometry provides a unified framework for understanding quantum secret sharing and contextuality, with tensor factorizations revealing geometric structures that govern both phenomena, offering new geometric insights into contextual configurations and practical applications in secret breaking protocols.

title: Grover Adaptive Search with Problem-Specific State Preparation
summary: Grover's search algorithm is one of the basic building block in the world of quantum algorithms. Successfully applying it to combinatorial optimization problems is a subtle challenge. As a quadratic speedup is not enough to naively search an exponentially large space, the search has to be complemented with a state preparation routine which increases the amplitudes of promising states by exploiting the problem structure. In this paper, we build upon previous work by Baertschi and Eidenbenz to construct heuristic state preparation routines for the Traveling Salesperson Problem (TSP), mimicking the well-known classical Lin-Kernighan heuristic. With our heuristic, we aim to achieve a reasonable approximation ratio with only a polynomial number of Grover iterations. Further, we compare several algorithmic settings relating to termination criteria and the choice of Grover iterations when the number of marked solutions is unknown.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes heuristic state preparation routines for Grover's algorithm applied to TSP, mimicking the classical Lin-Kernighan heuristic to achieve polynomial Grover iterations with reasonable approximation ratios.
AI.motivation: Grover's algorithm alone provides only quadratic speedup, which is insufficient for searching exponentially large combinatorial spaces like TSP. The paper aims to enhance Grover's search by incorporating problem-specific heuristics to amplify promising states more effectively.
AI.method: The authors build upon previous work by Baertschi and Eidenbenz to construct heuristic state preparation routines that mimic the classical Lin-Kernighan heuristic for TSP. They explore different algorithmic settings including termination criteria and strategies for handling unknown numbers of marked solutions.
AI.result: The paper aims to achieve reasonable approximation ratios for TSP using only a polynomial number of Grover iterations, rather than the exponential iterations required by naive Grover search on unstructured spaces.
AI.conclusion: By combining Grover's search with problem-specific heuristic state preparation inspired by classical algorithms, the approach enables more practical quantum solutions for combinatorial optimization problems like TSP with polynomial quantum resources.

title: Plethysm is in #BQP
summary:
Some representation-theoretic multiplicities, such as the Kostka and the Littlewood-Richardson coefficients, admit a combinatorial interpretation that places their computation in the complexity class #P. Whether this holds more generally is considered an important open problem in mathematics and computer science, with relevance for geometric complexity theory and quantum information. Recent work has investigated the quantum complexity of particular multiplicities, such as the Kronecker coefficients and certain special cases of the plethysm coefficients.
  Here, we show that a broad class of representation-theoretic multiplicities is in #BQP. In particular, our result implies that the plethysm coefficients are in #BQP, which was only known in special cases. It also implies all known results on the quantum complexity of previously studied coefficients as special cases, unifying, simplifying, and extending prior work. We obtain our result by multiple applications of the Schur transform. Recent work has improved its dependence on the local dimension, which is crucial for our work. We further describe a general approach for showing that representation-theoretic multiplicities are in #BQP that captures our approach as well as the approaches of prior work. We complement the above by showing that the same multiplicities are also naturally in GapP and obtain polynomial-time classical algorithms when certain parameters are fixed.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that a broad class of representation-theoretic multiplicities, including plethysm coefficients, are in the quantum complexity class #BQP, unifying and extending prior work on quantum complexity of representation theory.
AI.motivation: Understanding the computational complexity of representation-theoretic multiplicities (like Kostka, Littlewood-Richardson, Kronecker, and plethysm coefficients) is an important open problem with relevance to geometric complexity theory and quantum information. While some coefficients are known to be in #P, the quantum complexity of more general multiplicities remains open.
AI.method: The authors use multiple applications of the Schur transform, leveraging recent improvements in its dependence on local dimension. They develop a general approach for showing representation-theoretic multiplicities are in #BQP that captures both their method and prior work approaches.
AI.result: The paper demonstrates that a broad class of representation-theoretic multiplicities is in #BQP, specifically showing that plethysm coefficients are in #BQP (previously only known in special cases). The result unifies, simplifies, and extends all known results on quantum complexity of previously studied coefficients.
AI.conclusion: The work establishes that important representation-theoretic multiplicities have quantum polynomial-time algorithms, provides a unifying framework for understanding their quantum complexity, and complements these results by showing the same multiplicities are also in GapP with polynomial-time classical algorithms when certain parameters are fixed.

title: Non-Markovianity induced by Pauli-twirling
summary: Noise forms a central obstacle to effective quantum information processing. Recent experimental advances have enabled the tailoring of noise properties through Pauli twirling, transforming arbitrary noise channels into Pauli channels. This underpins theoretical descriptions of fault-tolerant quantum computation and forms an essential tool in noise characterization and error mitigation. Pauli-Lindblad channels have been introduced to aptly parameterize quasi-local Pauli errors across a quantum register, excluding negative Pauli-Lindblad parameters relying on the Markovianity of the underlying noise processes. We point out that caution is required when parameterizing channels as Pauli-Lindblad channels with nonnegative parameters. For this, we study the effects of Pauli twirling on Markovianity. We use the notion of Markovianity of a channel (rather than that of an entire semigroup) and prove a general Pauli channel is non-Markovian if and only if at least one of its Pauli-Lindblad parameters is negative. Using this, we show that Markovian quantum channels often become non-Markovian after Pauli twirling. The Pauli-twirling induced non-Markovianity necessitates the use of negative Pauli-Lindblad parameters for a correct noise description in experimentally realistic scenarios. An important example is the implementation of the $\sqrt{X}$-gate under standard Markovian noise. As such, our results have direct implications for quantum error mitigation protocols that rely on accurate noise characterization.

AI.tldr: Pauli twirling transforms arbitrary noise into Pauli channels but can induce non-Markovianity, requiring negative Pauli-Lindblad parameters for accurate noise characterization in realistic quantum systems.
AI.motivation: Noise characterization is crucial for quantum information processing. Pauli twirling is widely used to transform arbitrary noise into Pauli channels for theoretical descriptions and error mitigation, but the assumption that Pauli-Lindblad channels require nonnegative parameters relies on Markovianity assumptions that may not hold after twirling.
AI.method: The authors study the effects of Pauli twirling on Markovianity using the notion of Markovianity of a channel (rather than an entire semigroup). They prove that a general Pauli channel is non-Markovian if and only if at least one of its Pauli-Lindblad parameters is negative. They then show that Markovian quantum channels often become non-Markovian after Pauli twirling.
AI.result: Pauli twirling frequently induces non-Markovianity in originally Markovian channels, necessitating the use of negative Pauli-Lindblad parameters for accurate noise description. A key example is the implementation of the √X-gate under standard Markovian noise, which becomes non-Markovian after Pauli twirling.
AI.conclusion: Caution is required when parameterizing channels as Pauli-Lindblad channels with nonnegative parameters, as Pauli twirling often induces non-Markovianity. Negative Pauli-Lindblad parameters are necessary for correct noise characterization in experimentally realistic scenarios, with direct implications for quantum error mitigation protocols that rely on accurate noise models.

title: Classifying the simplest Bell inequalities beyond qubits and their applications towards self-testing
summary: Bell inequalities reveal the fundamentally nonlocal character of quantum mechanics. In this regard, one of the interesting problems is to explore all possible Bell inequalities that demonstrate a gap between local and nonlocal quantum behaviour. This is useful for the geometric characterisation of the set of nonlocal correlations achievable within quantum theory. Moreover, it provides a systematic way to construct Bell inequalities that are tailored to specific quantum information processing tasks. This characterisation is well understood in the simplest $(2,2,2)$ scenario, namely two parties performing two binary outcome measurements. However, beyond this setting, relatively few Bell inequalities are known, and the situation becomes particularly scarce in scenarios involving a greater number of outcomes. Here, we consider the $(2,2,3)$ scenario, or two parties performing two three-outcome measurements, and characterise all Bell inequalities that can arise from the simplest sum-of-squares decomposition and are maximally violated by the maximally entangled state of local dimension three. We then utilise them to self-test this state, along with a class of three-outcome measurements.

AI.tldr: Characterization of all Bell inequalities in the (2,2,3) scenario (two parties, two three-outcome measurements) that arise from sum-of-squares decompositions and are maximally violated by the 3-dimensional maximally entangled state, enabling self-testing of this state and measurement classes.
AI.motivation: To systematically explore Bell inequalities beyond the simplest (2,2,2) scenario, particularly in settings with more outcomes, for geometric characterization of quantum nonlocal correlations and construction of Bell inequalities tailored to specific quantum information tasks.
AI.method: Focus on the (2,2,3) scenario; characterize all Bell inequalities that can arise from the simplest sum-of-squares decomposition and are maximally violated by the maximally entangled state of local dimension three.
AI.result: Complete characterization of Bell inequalities in the (2,2,3) scenario from sum-of-squares decompositions, with maximal violation by the 3-dimensional maximally entangled state, enabling self-testing of both the state and a class of three-outcome measurements.
AI.conclusion: The work extends Bell inequality characterization beyond the simplest scenarios, providing tools for self-testing high-dimensional entangled states and measurements, with applications in quantum information processing and fundamental quantum theory.

title: A building block of quantum repeaters for scalable quantum networks
comment: Accepted for publication in Nature (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10177-4). This is the original submitted version
summary: Quantum networks, integrating quantum communication, quantum metrology, and distributed quantum computing, could provide secure and efficient information transfer, high-resolution sensing, and an exponential speed-up in information processing. Deterministic entanglement distribution over long distances is a prerequisite for scalable quantum networks, enabling the utilization of device-independent quantum key distribution (DI-QKD) and quantum teleportation to achieve secure and efficient information transfer. However, the exponential photon loss in optical fibres prohibits efficient and deterministic entanglement distribution. Quantum repeaters, incorporating entanglement swapping and entanglement purification with quantum memories, offer the most promising means to overcome this limitation in fibre-based quantum networks. Despite numerous pioneering efforts toward realizing quantum repeaters, a critical bottleneck remains, as remote memory-memory entanglement suffers from decoherence more rapidly than it can be established and purified over long distances. We overcome this by developing long-lived trapped-ion memories, an efficient telecom interface, and a high-visibility single-photon entanglement protocol. This allows us to establish and maintain memory-memory entanglement over a 10 km fibre within the average entanglement establishment time for the same distance. As a direct application, we demonstrate metropolitan-scale DI-QKD, distilling 1,917 secret keys out of 4.05*10^5 Bell pairs over 10 km. We further report a positive key rate over 101 km in the asymptotic limit, extending the achievable distance by more than two orders of magnitude. Our work provides a critical building block for quantum repeaters and marks an important step toward scalable quantum networks.

AI.tldr: Demonstration of metropolitan-scale quantum network with trapped-ion memories and telecom interface enabling memory-memory entanglement over 10 km fiber, achieving device-independent QKD over 10 km and positive key rate over 101 km.
AI.motivation: Quantum networks promise secure communication, high-resolution sensing, and exponential speed-up in information processing, but face fundamental limitations in deterministic entanglement distribution over long distances due to exponential photon loss in optical fibers. Quantum repeaters offer a solution but suffer from decoherence issues where remote memory-memory entanglement decays faster than it can be established and purified.
AI.method: Developed long-lived trapped-ion quantum memories, an efficient telecom interface, and a high-visibility single-photon entanglement protocol. This combination enables establishment and maintenance of memory-memory entanglement within the average entanglement establishment time for 10 km fiber distances.
AI.result: Successfully established and maintained memory-memory entanglement over 10 km fiber within the average entanglement establishment time. Demonstrated metropolitan-scale device-independent quantum key distribution (DI-QKD) with 1,917 secret keys distilled from 4.05×10^5 Bell pairs over 10 km. Achieved positive key rate over 101 km in the asymptotic limit, extending achievable distance by more than two orders of magnitude.
AI.conclusion: The work overcomes the critical bottleneck of decoherence in quantum repeaters by developing long-lived trapped-ion memories with telecom interface, enabling practical memory-memory entanglement over metropolitan distances. This represents a critical building block for quantum repeaters and marks significant progress toward scalable quantum networks.

title: Empirical Study of Observable Sets in Multiclass Quantum Classification
summary: Variational quantum algorithms have gained attention as early applications of quantum computers for learning tasks. In the context of supervised learning, most of the works that tackle classification problems with parameterized quantum circuits constrain their scope to the setting of binary classification or perform multiclass classification via ensembles of binary classifiers (strategies such as one versus rest). Those few works that propose native multiclass models, however, do not justify the choice of observables that perform the classification. This work studies two main classification criteria in multiclass quantum machine learning: maximizing the expected value of an observable representing a class or maximizing the fidelity of the encoded quantum state with a reference state representing a class. To compare both approaches, sets of Pauli strings and sets of projectors into the computational basis are chosen as observables in the quantum machine learning models. Observing the empirical behavior of each model type, the effect of different observable set choices on the performance of quantum machine learning models is analyzed in the context of Barren Plateaus and Neural Collapse. The results provide insights that may guide the design of future multiclass quantum machine learning models.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes two multiclass classification approaches in quantum machine learning: maximizing expected values of class-representing observables versus maximizing fidelity with class-representing reference states, comparing Pauli strings and computational basis projectors as observables.
AI.motivation: Most quantum classification work focuses on binary classification or uses ensembles for multiclass problems. Few native multiclass models exist, and those that do lack justification for their observable choices. The paper aims to systematically compare classification criteria and observable selections to guide future multiclass QML model design.
AI.method: The study compares two multiclass classification criteria: 1) maximizing expected values of observables representing classes, and 2) maximizing fidelity of encoded quantum states with reference states representing classes. Two types of observable sets are examined: sets of Pauli strings and sets of projectors into the computational basis. The analysis evaluates empirical behavior, effects on performance, and examines these approaches in the context of Barren Plateaus and Neural Collapse phenomena.
AI.result: The paper provides empirical observations of each model type's behavior and analyzes how different observable set choices affect quantum machine learning model performance. The results offer insights into the trade-offs between the two classification approaches and observable selections, particularly regarding their susceptibility to Barren Plateaus and Neural Collapse phenomena.
AI.conclusion: The comparative analysis of multiclass classification criteria and observable choices provides valuable insights that can guide the design of future multiclass quantum machine learning models, addressing the current gap in justified observable selection for native multiclass QML approaches.

title: Intelligent Control of Collisional Architectures for Deterministic Multipartite State Engineering
summary: Designing scalable, noise-tolerant control protocols for multipartite entanglement is a central challenge for quantum technologies, and it naturally calls for \emph{algorithmic} synthesis of interaction parameters rather than handcrafted gate sequences. Here we introduce an intelligent, constraint-aware control framework for deterministic generation of symmetric Dicke states $|D_n^{(m)}\rangle$ in repeated-interaction (collision-model) architectures. The protocol employs excitation-preserving partial-SWAP collisions between two disjoint qubit registers, mediated by $m$ ancillary ``shuttle'' qubits, and poses Dicke-state preparation as a \emph{closed-loop design} problem: given the target $(n,m)$, automatically infer collision strengths that maximize fidelity under practical constraints. Concretely, we formulate a two-parameter, bound-constrained optimization over intra-register and shuttle--register collision angles and solve it using a multi-start strategy with L-BFGS-B, yielding a reproducible controller prescription (optimized $γ_{\mathrm{in}}$, $γ_{\mathrm{sh}}$, and minimal-round convergence points) for each target. This removes the need for projective measurements and extends collisional entanglement generation beyond the single-excitation (W-state) sector to arbitrary $m$. Crucially, we optimize \emph{within} imperfect collisional dynamics where errors act throughout the sequence, including stochastic interaction dropouts (missing collisions) and standard decoherence channels. Strikingly, across wide error ranges the optimized controller preserves high preparation fidelity; imperfections manifest primarily as a modest increase in the required number of collision rounds. This behavior reflects a tunable competition in which noise suppresses correlations while properly chosen collisions continuously replenish them, allowing the control algorithm to trade time for fidelity.

AI.tldr: Algorithmic synthesis of collision strengths for deterministic Dicke state generation in repeated-interaction architectures, optimized under practical constraints and noise.
AI.motivation: Scalable, noise-tolerant control protocols for multipartite entanglement require algorithmic synthesis rather than handcrafted gate sequences, particularly for deterministic generation of symmetric Dicke states in practical quantum architectures.
AI.method: Closed-loop design framework using excitation-preserving partial-SWAP collisions between two disjoint qubit registers mediated by ancillary shuttle qubits. Formulates two-parameter bound-constrained optimization over intra-register and shuttle-register collision angles, solved using multi-start strategy with L-BFGS-B algorithm.
AI.result: Reproducible controller prescriptions (optimized collision angles and minimal-round convergence points) for arbitrary Dicke states beyond single-excitation W-states. High preparation fidelity preserved across wide error ranges including stochastic interaction dropouts and standard decoherence channels, with imperfections mainly increasing required collision rounds.
AI.conclusion: The framework enables noise-tolerant, algorithmic synthesis of entanglement protocols that trade time for fidelity, removing need for projective measurements and extending collisional entanglement generation to arbitrary Dicke states under practical constraints.

title: Time resolution at the quantum limit of two incoherent sources based on frequency resolved two-photon-interference
summary: The Rayleigh criterion is a widely known limit in the resolution of incoherent sources with classical measurements in the spatial domain. Unsurprisingly the estimation of the time delay between two weak incoherent signals is afflicted by an analogue problem. In this work, we show the emergence of two-photon quantum beats in the frequency domain from the interference at a beam splitter of a photon emitted by a reference source and one from the two incoherent weak signals. We demonstrate, based on this phenomena, that with a relatively low number of measurements of the frequencies of the interfering photons either bunching or antibunching at the beam splitter output one can achieve a precision amounting to half of the quantum limit, independently of both the temporal shape of the photonic wavepacket and the time delay to be estimated. The feasibility of the technique makes it applicable in astronomy, microscopy, remote clocks synchronization and radar ranging

AI.tldr: Two-photon quantum beats enable sub-Rayleigh time delay estimation with half the quantum limit precision, independent of wavepacket shape and delay magnitude
AI.motivation: Overcome the Rayleigh criterion limitation in estimating time delays between weak incoherent signals, analogous to spatial resolution limits
AI.method: Use two-photon quantum beats from interference at a beam splitter between a reference photon and photons from two incoherent weak signals, measuring frequencies of interfering photons showing bunching/antibunching
AI.result: Achieve precision amounting to half of the quantum limit with relatively few measurements, independent of photonic wavepacket temporal shape and time delay magnitude
AI.conclusion: Feasible technique applicable to astronomy, microscopy, remote clock synchronization, and radar ranging for sub-Rayleigh time delay estimation

title: Quantum Charging Advantage in Superconducting Solid-State Batteries
summary: Quantum battery, as a novel energy storage device, offers the potential for unprecedented efficiency and performance beyond the capabilities of classical systems, with broad implications for future quantum technologies. Here, we experimentally \RefC{demonstrate quantum charging advantage (QCA)} in a scalable solid-state quantum battery. More specifically, we show how double-excitation Hamiltonians for two-level systems promote scalable QCA \RefB{with standard methods.} We effectively implement the collective evolution of quantum systems with 2 up to 12 battery cells in a superconducting quantum processor, and study the performance of quantum charging compared to its uncorrelated classical counterpart. The model considered is a linear chain of superconducting transmon qubits with only \textit{nearest-neighbor} and \textit{pairwise} interactions, which constitute the simplest model of a multi-cell quantum battery. Our results empirically realize substantial QCA without the necessity of adopting long-range and many-body interactions \RefB{ and showcase the quantum features of the QB charging processes with measurements of non-zero coherent ergotropy, incoherent ergotropy and entanglement,} revealing a promising prospect for further developments of efficient and experimentally feasible protocols for QCA.

AI.tldr: Experimental demonstration of quantum charging advantage in a scalable solid-state quantum battery using superconducting qubits, showing substantial advantage without requiring long-range or many-body interactions.
AI.motivation: Quantum batteries offer potential for unprecedented efficiency beyond classical systems, but experimental demonstrations of quantum charging advantage in scalable solid-state systems are needed to advance practical quantum technologies.
AI.method: Implemented collective evolution of quantum systems with 2-12 battery cells in a superconducting quantum processor using linear chain of transmon qubits with nearest-neighbor pairwise interactions, studying quantum charging vs. uncorrelated classical counterpart.
AI.result: Successfully demonstrated substantial quantum charging advantage without requiring long-range or many-body interactions, with measurements showing non-zero coherent ergotropy, incoherent ergotropy, and entanglement in the charging processes.
AI.conclusion: The work reveals promising prospects for developing efficient and experimentally feasible protocols for quantum charging advantage in scalable solid-state quantum batteries, advancing practical quantum energy storage technologies.

title: Representation theory of inhomogeneous Gaussian unitaries
summary: Gaussian unitaries, generated by quadratic Hamiltonians, are fundamental in quantum optics and continuous-variable computing. Their structures correspond to symplectic (bosons) and orthogonal (fermions) groups, but physical realizations give rise to their respective double covers, introducing phase and sign ambiguities. The homogeneous (quadratic-only) case has been resolved through a parameterization constructed in a recent work [arXiv:2409.11628]. We extend the previous framework to inhomogeneous Gaussian unitaries parameterized by $(M,z,Ψ)$. The Baker-Campbel-Hausdorff formula allows us then to factor any Gaussian unitary into a squeezing and a displacement transformation, from which we derive the group multiplication law.

AI.tldr: Extension of parameterization framework from homogeneous to inhomogeneous Gaussian unitaries, enabling factorization into squeezing and displacement transformations with derived group multiplication law.
AI.motivation: Gaussian unitaries are fundamental in quantum optics and continuous-variable quantum computing, but physical realizations introduce phase/sign ambiguities due to double covers. While homogeneous (quadratic-only) case was resolved in prior work, the inhomogeneous case needed systematic treatment.
AI.method: Extends previous framework to inhomogeneous Gaussian unitaries parameterized by (M,z,Ψ). Uses Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff formula to factor any Gaussian unitary into squeezing and displacement transformations, then derives the group multiplication law.
AI.result: Complete parameterization of inhomogeneous Gaussian unitaries, factorization theorem showing decomposition into squeezing and displacement components, and explicit group multiplication law for these transformations.
AI.conclusion: Provides comprehensive mathematical framework for inhomogeneous Gaussian unitaries, resolving phase/sign ambiguities in physical realizations and enabling systematic analysis of these fundamental quantum operations in continuous-variable systems.

title: Weak forms offer strong regularisations: how to make physics-informed (quantum) machine learning more robust
summary: Physics-informed (PI) methodologies have surged to become a pillar route to solve Differential Equations (DEs), sustained by the growth of machine learning methods in scientific contexts. The main proposition of PI is to minimise variationally a loss function, formally ensuring that a neural surrogate of the solution has the DE locally satisfied. The nature of such formulation encouraged the exploration of equivalent quantum algorithms, where the surrogate solution is expressed by variational quantum architectures. The locality of typical loss functions emphasises the DE to hold at an ensemble of points sampled in the domain, but encounters issues when generalising beyond such points, or when propagating boundary conditions. Issues which affect classical and quantum PI algorithms alike. The quest to fill this gap in robustness and accuracy against mainstream DE solvers has led to a plethora of proposals in various directions. In particular, classical DE solvers have long employed the weak form - an integral based approach aiming at imposing a global condition on the solution - prioritising a good average behaviour instead of ``overfitting'' select points. Here, we propose and explore to combine contributions from both local and global loss functions in PI routines, to exploit the advantages and mitigate the weaknesses of both. We showcase this intuition in a variety of problems focusing on differentiable quantum architectures, and demonstrating in particular how orchestrating such hybrid loss formulation with domain decomposition can offer a strong advantage over local-only strategies.

AI.tldr: Proposes hybrid physics-informed approach combining local and global loss functions for solving differential equations using quantum architectures, demonstrating advantages over local-only strategies through domain decomposition.
AI.motivation: Physics-informed methods for solving differential equations face issues with generalization beyond sampled points and boundary condition propagation. Classical weak form approaches prioritize global behavior over point-wise fitting, suggesting a need to combine local and global strategies for improved robustness and accuracy.
AI.method: Combines contributions from both local and global loss functions in physics-informed routines, orchestrating hybrid loss formulation with domain decomposition. Uses differentiable quantum architectures as surrogate solutions, applying this approach to various problems.
AI.result: Demonstrates that hybrid loss formulation with domain decomposition offers strong advantages over local-only strategies, showing improved performance in solving differential equations using quantum architectures.
AI.conclusion: Integrating local and global loss functions in physics-informed quantum algorithms addresses limitations of point-wise approaches, providing more robust and accurate solutions to differential equations through balanced optimization strategies.

title: Non-Hermitian Renormalization Group from a Few-Body Perspective
summary: Non-Hermiticity plays a fundamental role in open quantum systems and describes a wide variety of effects of interactions with environments, including quantum measurement. However, understanding its consequences in strongly interacting systems is still elusive due to the interplay between non-perturbative strong correlations and non-Hermiticity. While the Wilsonian renormalization group (RG) method has been applied to tackle this problem, its foundation, based on the existence of the partition function, is ill-defined. In this paper, we establish a microscopic foundation of the non-Hermitian RG method from a few-body perspective. We show that the invariance of the scattering amplitude under RG transformations enables us to rigorously derive the non-Hermitian RG equation, giving a physically transparent interpretation of RG flows. We discuss a detailed structure of such RG flows in a non-relativistic two-body system with inelastic two-body loss, and show its relation to a non-Hermitian quantum scale anomaly. Our analysis suggests that non-Hermitian complex potentials often used in high-energy physics can be interpreted as being caused by quantum measurement, where the detection of elastically scattered particles updates the observer's knowledge, resulting in a nonunitary state change of the system. We apply our formalism to nuclear physics, find the emergence of a critical semicircle, and show that several nuclei are located near the critical semicircle in the coherent neutron-nucleus scattering. We also propose that the localized dineutron in two-neutron halo nuclei can be interpreted as the quantum measurement effect on the imaginary potential associated with absorption into the core nucleus. Our result bridges different contexts of non-Hermitian systems in high-energy and atomic, molecular, and optical physics, opening an interdisciplinary playground of non-Hermitian few-body physics.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes a microscopic foundation for non-Hermitian renormalization group methods from a few-body perspective, connecting non-Hermitian complex potentials to quantum measurement effects and applying the formalism to nuclear physics.
AI.motivation: Non-Hermiticity is fundamental in open quantum systems but understanding its consequences in strongly interacting systems remains elusive due to the interplay between non-perturbative strong correlations and non-Hermiticity. Traditional Wilsonian RG methods have ill-defined foundations for non-Hermitian systems.
AI.method: Established a microscopic foundation for non-Hermitian RG from a few-body perspective using invariance of scattering amplitude under RG transformations to rigorously derive non-Hermitian RG equations. Applied formalism to non-relativistic two-body systems with inelastic two-body loss and nuclear physics contexts.
AI.result: Derived physically transparent interpretation of RG flows, revealed relation to non-Hermitian quantum scale anomaly, showed non-Hermitian complex potentials can be interpreted as quantum measurement effects, found emergence of critical semicircle in nuclear physics, and showed several nuclei are located near critical semicircle in coherent neutron-nucleus scattering.
AI.conclusion: The work bridges different contexts of non-Hermitian systems in high-energy and atomic/molecular/optical physics, opening an interdisciplinary playground for non-Hermitian few-body physics, with implications for interpreting localized dineutron in two-neutron halo nuclei as quantum measurement effects.

title: Heterogeneous Optically-Detected Spin-Acoustic Resonance in Solid-State Molecular Thin-film
summary: We report an implementation of spin-acoustic resonance in pentacene thin films integrated on a high-quality-factor (high-Q) surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonator on a lithium niobate substrate. Heterogeneous optically detected spin-acoustic resonance (HODSAR) is an optically detected spin-resonance measurement in which the resonant drive is delivered mechanically by a surface acoustic wave (SAW). By leveraging the photo-excited triplet state of pentacene at room temperature, we demonstrate coherent spin manipulation via acoustic driving under zero externally applied magnetic field. The heterogeneously integrated device, referred to as HODSAR, utilizes spin-phonon coupling to achieve mechanically driven, zero-field spin resonance, opening avenues for room-temperature mechanically addressable spin control and device integration. We show that the high-Q multimode response of the SAW resonator enables spectrally selective acoustic addressing of triplet transitions near 105 MHz. Coherent control is evidenced by Rabi oscillations, with a Rabi frequency that increases linearly with the square root of the applied RF input power over the measured drive range, consistent with driven two-level dynamics under acoustic excitation. These results establish spin-acoustic resonance in a heterogeneously integrated molecular thin-film platform and provide a quantitative basis for benchmarking mechanically mediated spin control.

AI.tldr: Implementation of spin-acoustic resonance in pentacene thin films on high-Q SAW resonators enables optically detected, mechanically driven spin manipulation at room temperature without external magnetic fields.
AI.motivation: To develop room-temperature mechanically addressable spin control by leveraging spin-phonon coupling in heterogeneously integrated molecular thin-film platforms, enabling device integration without requiring external magnetic fields.
AI.method: Heterogeneous optically detected spin-acoustic resonance (HODSAR) using pentacene thin films integrated on high-quality-factor surface acoustic wave resonators on lithium niobate substrates, utilizing photo-excited triplet states and spin-phonon coupling for acoustic driving.
AI.result: Demonstrated coherent spin manipulation via acoustic driving at zero external magnetic field, showing spectrally selective acoustic addressing of triplet transitions near 105 MHz using high-Q multimode SAW response, with Rabi oscillations showing linear increase of Rabi frequency with square root of RF input power.
AI.conclusion: Established spin-acoustic resonance in heterogeneously integrated molecular thin-film platform, providing quantitative basis for benchmarking mechanically mediated spin control and opening avenues for room-temperature mechanically addressable spin devices.

title: The equivalence of quantum deletion and insertion errors on permutation-invariant codes
summary: Quantum synchronisation errors are a class of quantum errors that change the number of qubits in a quantum system. The classical error correction of synchronisation errors has been well-studied, including an insertion-deletion equivalence more than a half-century ago, but little progress has been made towards the quantum counterpart since the birth of quantum error correction. We address the longstanding problem of a quantum insertion-deletion equivalence on permutation-invariant codes, detailing the conditions under which such codes are $t$-insertion error-correctable. We extend these conditions to quantum insdel errors, formulating a more restrictive set of conditions under which permutation-invariant codes are $(t,s)$-insdel error-correctable. Our work resolves many of the outstanding questions regarding the quantum error correction of synchronisation errors.

AI.tldr: Quantum insertion-deletion equivalence established for permutation-invariant codes, resolving longstanding synchronization error correction problems.
AI.motivation: Quantum synchronization errors (changing qubit count) lack quantum error correction progress despite classical insertion-deletion equivalence being established over 50 years ago.
AI.method: Analyze permutation-invariant codes, establish conditions for t-insertion error-correctability, extend to more restrictive conditions for (t,s)-insdel error-correctability.
AI.result: Quantum insertion-deletion equivalence proven for permutation-invariant codes, with specific conditions determining error-correctability for insertion and combined insertion-deletion errors.
AI.conclusion: Resolves longstanding quantum synchronization error correction problems by establishing quantum insertion-deletion equivalence and error-correctability conditions for permutation-invariant codes.

title: High-Probability Heralded Entanglement via Repeated Spin-Photon Phase Encoding with Moderate Cooperativity
summary: We propose a heralded high-probability scheme to generate remote entanglement between moderate-cooperativity spin-cavity registers with high fidelity. In conventional single-shot interfaces, limited cooperativity restricts the spin-conditional optical response and thus strongly suppresses the success probability. Our proposal instead recycles a single incident photon for repeated interactions with the spin-cavity register, such that a small spin-conditional phase shift acquired on each round trip accumulates coherently to enable remote entanglement. Moreover, the repeated scheme enables higher spin-photon encoding efficiency by using a spectral-width-scaling photon pulse with a shorter duration. We show that, for realistic imperfections and losses, this repeated phase-encoding approach produces high-fidelity entangled states with an appreciable success probability even at cooperativity $C\sim1$. Our protocol is particularly well suited to weakly coupled, cavity-based solid-state spin platforms and provides a route toward hybrid, photon-loss-tolerant distributed quantum computing.

AI.tldr: Repeated photon-spin interactions enable high-fidelity remote entanglement generation even at low cooperativity (C∼1) by accumulating small phase shifts coherently.
AI.motivation: Conventional single-shot interfaces suffer from low success probability due to limited cooperativity restricting spin-conditional optical response. Need better approach for weakly coupled, cavity-based solid-state spin platforms.
AI.method: Recycles single incident photon for repeated interactions with spin-cavity register, allowing small spin-conditional phase shifts to accumulate coherently. Uses spectral-width-scaling photon pulses with shorter duration for higher encoding efficiency.
AI.result: Produces high-fidelity entangled states with appreciable success probability even at cooperativity C∼1, despite realistic imperfections and losses.
AI.conclusion: Protocol is well-suited for weakly coupled solid-state spin platforms and provides route toward hybrid, photon-loss-tolerant distributed quantum computing.

title: Spin-active chlorine-related centers in 4H-SiC with telecom-band emissions
summary: A photoluminescence (PL) and magnetic resonance investigation of a defect in chlorine-implanted 4H-SiC is presented. This Cl-related center emits light at telecom wavelengths with zero-phonon lines in the range 1350-1540 nm. Its four configurations exhibit stable PL spectra characterized by narrow zero-phonon lines. For the two configurations that emit light at the C-band, a Debye-Waller factor in the range 22-25% is estimated. Optically detected magnetic resonance confirms that the Cl-related center is spin active and stable at room temperature with the zero-field splitting in the range of 1.0-1.4 GHz. The combined optical and spin properties suggest this center to be a highly promising candidate for scalable quantum networks.

AI.tldr: A Cl-related defect in 4H-SiC emits telecom-wavelength light with narrow zero-phonon lines, shows spin activity with room-temperature stability, and is promising for quantum networks.
AI.motivation: To investigate a chlorine-related defect in 4H-SiC for its potential as a quantum emitter, particularly for telecom-wavelength applications in quantum networks.
AI.method: Used photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy and optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) to study chlorine-implanted 4H-SiC samples, analyzing optical emission properties and spin characteristics.
AI.result: The Cl-related center emits at telecom wavelengths (1350-1540 nm) with narrow zero-phonon lines, has four configurations, shows 22-25% Debye-Waller factor for C-band emitters, exhibits spin activity with 1.0-1.4 GHz zero-field splitting, and remains stable at room temperature.
AI.conclusion: The defect's combined optical properties (telecom emission) and spin characteristics (room-temperature stability) make it a highly promising candidate for scalable quantum network applications.

title: High-brightness fiber-based Sagnac source of entangled photon pairs for multiplexed quantum networks
summary: A fully fibered source of entangled photon pairs based on a nonlinear Sagnac interferometer is reported. Operating at telecom wavelengths, the source relies exclusively on standard fiber-optic components and periodically poled lithium niobate (PPLN) waveguides, resulting in a compact, robust, and field-deployable architecture. The generation stage supports both polarization and energy-time entanglement without modification, enabling versatile operation depending on the targeted application. Broadband spontaneous parametric down-conversion allows dense wavelength-division multiplexing over the telecom C and L bands. High normalized brightness (10.3 kpairs/s/nm/mW$^2$) is achieved on a standard 100 GHz ITU channel pair, together with high entanglement quality. Polarization and energy-time encodings are characterized through state tomography and two-photon interference measurements, yielding fidelities, purities, and visibilities exceeding 96 % over multiple wavelength channels. The stability and reproducibility of the source are further evaluated through long-duration operation in a network environment. These results demonstrate that the proposed Sagnac source constitutes a practical and scalable building block for future plug-and-play quantum communication and quantum networking platforms.

AI.tldr: A fiber-based entangled photon pair source using a Sagnac interferometer with PPLN waveguides achieves high brightness and entanglement quality at telecom wavelengths for quantum communication applications.
AI.motivation: To develop a practical, field-deployable entangled photon source using standard fiber-optic components for scalable quantum communication and networking platforms.
AI.method: A fully fibered Sagnac interferometer architecture using periodically poled lithium niobate (PPLN) waveguides for spontaneous parametric down-conversion, supporting both polarization and energy-time entanglement without modification.
AI.result: Achieved high normalized brightness (10.3 kpairs/s/nm/mW²) on 100 GHz ITU channels, with entanglement fidelities, purities, and visibilities exceeding 96% over multiple wavelength channels in telecom C and L bands.
AI.conclusion: The Sagnac source is a practical, scalable building block for plug-and-play quantum communication and networking platforms, demonstrating robustness, stability, and versatility.

title: A cavity-mediated reconfigurable coupling scheme for superconducting qubits
summary: Superconducting qubits have achieved remarkable progress in gate fidelity and coherence, yet their typical nearest-neighbor connectivity presents constraints for implementing complex quantum circuits. Here, we introduce a cavity-mediated coupling architecture in which a shared cavity mode, accessed through tunable qubit-cavity couplers, enables dynamically reconfigurable interactions between non-adjacent qubits. By selectively activating the couplers, we demonstrate that high-fidelity iSWAP and CZ gates can be performed within 50 ns with simulated coherent error below $10^{-4}$, while residual $ZZ$ interaction during idling remains below a few kilohertz. Extending to a four-qubit system, we also simulate gates between every qubit pair by selectively enabling the couplers with low qubit crosstalk. This approach provides a practical route toward enhanced interaction flexibility in superconducting quantum processors and may serve as a useful building block for devices that benefit from selective non-local coupling.

AI.tldr: A cavity-mediated coupling architecture enables dynamically reconfigurable interactions between non-adjacent superconducting qubits using tunable qubit-cavity couplers, achieving high-fidelity gates with low crosstalk.
AI.motivation: Superconducting qubits have achieved high gate fidelity and coherence, but their typical nearest-neighbor connectivity limits implementation of complex quantum circuits that require interactions between non-adjacent qubits.
AI.method: Introduces a cavity-mediated coupling architecture where a shared cavity mode is accessed through tunable qubit-cavity couplers, enabling selective activation of interactions between non-adjacent qubits through the cavity.
AI.result: Demonstrates high-fidelity iSWAP and CZ gates within 50 ns with simulated coherent error below 10^-4, residual ZZ interaction during idling below a few kHz, and successful simulation of gates between every qubit pair in a four-qubit system with low crosstalk.
AI.conclusion: This approach provides a practical route toward enhanced interaction flexibility in superconducting quantum processors and serves as a useful building block for devices benefiting from selective non-local coupling.

title: Differentiable Logical Programming for Quantum Circuit Discovery and Optimization
summary: Designing high-fidelity quantum circuits remains challenging, and current paradigms often depend on heuristic, fixed-ansatz structures or rule-based compilers that can be suboptimal or lack generality. We introduce a neuro-symbolic framework that reframes quantum circuit design as a differentiable logic programming problem. Our model represents a scaffold of potential quantum gates and parameterized operations as a set of learnable, continuous ``truth values'' or ``switches,'' $s \in [0, 1]^N$. These switches are optimized via standard gradient descent to satisfy a user-defined set of differentiable, logical axioms (e.g., correctness, simplicity, robustness). We provide a theoretical formulation bridging continuous logic (via T-norms) and unitary evolution (via geodesic interpolation), while addressing the barren plateau problem through biased initialization. We illustrate the approach on tasks including discovery of a 4-qubit Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT) from a scaffold of 21 candidate gates. We also report a hardware-aware adaptation experiment on the 133-qubit IBM Torino processor, where the method improved fidelity by 59.3 percentage points in a localized routing task while adapting to hardware failures.

AI.tldr: Neuro-symbolic framework for quantum circuit design using differentiable logic programming with learnable gate switches optimized via gradient descent to satisfy logical constraints.
AI.motivation: Current quantum circuit design methods rely on heuristic, fixed-ansatz structures or rule-based compilers that are often suboptimal and lack generality, creating a need for more systematic and adaptable approaches.
AI.method: Represents quantum circuit design as differentiable logic programming with learnable continuous switches (s ∈ [0,1]^N) for potential gates, optimized via gradient descent to satisfy differentiable logical axioms, bridging continuous logic (T-norms) and unitary evolution (geodesic interpolation) while addressing barren plateaus with biased initialization.
AI.result: Successfully discovered a 4-qubit Quantum Fourier Transform from a scaffold of 21 candidate gates, and achieved 59.3 percentage point fidelity improvement in hardware-aware adaptation on IBM Torino processor while adapting to hardware failures.
AI.conclusion: The neuro-symbolic framework provides a systematic, differentiable approach to quantum circuit design that can discover optimal circuits from candidate gates and adapt to hardware constraints, offering a promising alternative to heuristic methods.

title: Error compensation without a time penalty: robust spin-lock-induced crossing in solution NMR
summary: A modification of the widely-used spin-lock-induced crossing (SLIC) procedure is proposed for the solution nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) of strongly coupled nuclear spin systems, including singlet NMR and parahydrogen-enhanced hyperpolarised NMR experiments. The compensated-SLIC (cSLIC) scheme uses a repetitive sequence where the repeated element employs two different radiofrequency field amplitudes. Effective compensation for deviations in the radiofrequency field amplitude is achieved without increasing the overall duration of the SLIC sequence. The advantageous properties of cSLIC are demonstrated by numerical simulations and by representative experiments.

AI.tldr: A compensated-SLIC (cSLIC) method is proposed for NMR of strongly coupled spin systems, using alternating RF field amplitudes to compensate for RF amplitude deviations without increasing sequence duration.
AI.motivation: The standard SLIC procedure for NMR of strongly coupled nuclear spin systems suffers from sensitivity to radiofrequency field amplitude deviations, which can degrade performance in applications like singlet NMR and parahydrogen-enhanced hyperpolarized NMR experiments.
AI.method: A modified SLIC sequence called compensated-SLIC (cSLIC) uses a repetitive sequence where each repeated element employs two different radiofrequency field amplitudes. This design compensates for RF field amplitude deviations without increasing the overall sequence duration compared to standard SLIC.
AI.result: The cSLIC scheme demonstrates effective compensation for radiofrequency field amplitude deviations. Its advantageous properties are validated through both numerical simulations and representative experimental demonstrations.
AI.conclusion: The cSLIC method provides improved robustness against RF field amplitude variations for NMR experiments on strongly coupled spin systems, offering benefits for singlet NMR and parahydrogen-enhanced hyperpolarized NMR applications without extending experimental time.

title: Multiplexed microwave resonators by frequency comb spectroscopy
comment: 4 main figures and 5 others in the appendices
summary: Coplanar waveguide resonators are central to the thriving field of circuit quantum electrodynamics. Recently, we have demonstrated the generation of a broadband microwave-frequency comb spectrum using a superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID) driven by a time-dependent magnetic field. Here, the frequency comb is used to spectroscopically probe a bank of coplanar microwave resonators, inductively coupled to a common transmission line, a standard circuit with a variety of applications. We compare the resonator line shape obtained from signals synthesized at room temperature using conventional electronics with the radiation produced in the cryogenic environment by our source, showing substantial equivalence in the estimation of the resonator quality factors. To measure non-uniformly spaced resonant frequencies, we drive the generator with a bi-chromatic tone to generate intermodulation products. Such a dense frequency comb spectrum enables simultaneous addressing of a few resonators via frequency multiplexing. Finally, we discuss the criteria for achieving effective spectroscopic coverage of a given frequency bandwidth.

AI.tldr: A superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID) generates a broadband microwave frequency comb for spectroscopic probing of coplanar waveguide resonators, enabling simultaneous measurement of multiple resonators via frequency multiplexing.
AI.motivation: Coplanar waveguide resonators are fundamental to circuit quantum electrodynamics, and there's a need for efficient spectroscopic methods to probe multiple resonators simultaneously, particularly those with non-uniform frequency spacing.
AI.method: Using a SQUID driven by time-dependent magnetic fields to generate broadband microwave frequency combs, then applying these combs to spectroscopically probe a bank of coplanar microwave resonators inductively coupled to a common transmission line. For non-uniformly spaced resonators, a bi-chromatic drive generates intermodulation products to create dense frequency comb spectra.
AI.result: The frequency comb spectroscopy shows substantial equivalence to conventional room-temperature signal synthesis in estimating resonator quality factors. The dense frequency comb enables simultaneous addressing of multiple resonators via frequency multiplexing, even for non-uniformly spaced resonant frequencies.
AI.conclusion: SQUID-generated microwave frequency combs provide an effective cryogenic spectroscopic tool for probing coplanar waveguide resonators, with criteria established for achieving comprehensive spectroscopic coverage of given frequency bandwidths.

title: GHz-rate polarization-based QKD system for fiber and satellite applications
summary:
Quantum key distribution (QKD) leverages the principles of quantum mechanics to exchange a secret key between two parties. Despite its promising features, QKD also faces several practical challenges such as transmission loss, noise in quantum channels and finite key size effects. Addressing these issues is crucial for the large-scale deployment of QKD in fiber and satellite networks.
  In this paper, we present a 1550 nm QKD system realizing the efficient-BB84 protocol and based on the iPOGNAC scheme. The system achieved repetition rates up to 1.5~GHz and showed an intrinsic QBER of $\sim 0.4\%$. The system was first tested on a laboratory fiber link and then on an intermodal link in the field, consisting of both deployed fiber and a 620 m free-space channel. The experiment was performed in daylight conditions, exploiting the Qubit4Sync synchronization protocol. With this trial, we achieved a new benchmark for free-space BB84 QKD systems by generating a sustained secret key rate (SKR) above 1~Mb/s for 1 hour. Finally, exploiting a recently discovered finite-size bound, we achieved a secure key rate of about 10 Mb/s at low losses (5 dB), and around 6.5~kb/s in the high-loss (38.5 dB), low block length ($N=10^4$) regime. The latter results demonstrate the system's suitability for highly lossy and time-constrained scenarios such as QKD from low Earth orbit satellites.

AI.tldr: A 1550 nm QKD system implementing efficient-BB84 protocol achieves 1.5 GHz repetition rates, demonstrates 1+ Mb/s secret key rates in free-space field tests, and shows suitability for satellite QKD applications through finite-size analysis.
AI.motivation: To address practical challenges in QKD deployment including transmission loss, quantum channel noise, and finite key size effects, particularly for large-scale deployment in fiber and satellite networks.
AI.method: Implemented a 1550 nm QKD system using the efficient-BB84 protocol based on the iPOGNAC scheme, tested on both laboratory fiber links and intermodal field links (deployed fiber + 620 m free-space channel) with daylight operation using Qubit4Sync synchronization protocol.
AI.result: Achieved repetition rates up to 1.5 GHz with intrinsic QBER ~0.4%; generated sustained SKR above 1 Mb/s for 1 hour in free-space field tests; obtained secure key rates of ~10 Mb/s at 5 dB loss and ~6.5 kb/s at 38.5 dB loss with N=10^4 block length using finite-size analysis.
AI.conclusion: The system demonstrates high-performance QKD suitable for practical deployment, particularly in lossy and time-constrained scenarios like low Earth orbit satellite communications, setting new benchmarks for free-space BB84 QKD systems.

title: Long distance quantum illumination and ranging using polarization entangled photon pairs in a lossy environment
summary: Using polarization entangled photon pairs, we demonstrate a robust scheme for quantum illumination and ranging in a lossy environment. Entangled photon pairs are generated in a Sagnac interferometer configuration, yielding high-visibility two-photon polarization entanglement with a measured CHSH parameter of $S =2.802\pm0.002$. One of the photons from the entangled pair is retained as idler and the other one is directed into either of the two paths, namely reference and probe, of which probe is sent toward a distant object through a lossy free-space channel, and the reflected photons are collected after round-trip free-space propagation over distances approaching $1$ km. Remarkably, strong correlations are observed with CHSH values $S >2.6$ even when only a few tens of probe photons are returned, confirming the robustness of polarization entanglement under long-distance free-space propagation. This work reports the robustness of encoding photons in different basis before it is sent towards the object and recovery of polarization entanglement even after a kilometer-scale scattering from the objects, establishing a practical foundation for scalable quantum-assisted object detection and ranging.

AI.tldr: Demonstration of robust quantum illumination and ranging using polarization-entangled photon pairs over kilometer-scale free-space distances in lossy environments.
AI.motivation: To establish a practical foundation for scalable quantum-assisted object detection and ranging by demonstrating the robustness of polarization entanglement under long-distance free-space propagation in lossy environments.
AI.method: Generate polarization-entangled photon pairs using a Sagnac interferometer configuration, with one photon retained as idler and the other sent as probe toward distant objects through lossy free-space channels up to 1 km. Measure CHSH parameter to quantify entanglement quality before and after propagation.
AI.result: Achieved high-visibility two-photon polarization entanglement with measured CHSH parameter S = 2.802 ± 0.002. Maintained strong correlations with CHSH values S > 2.6 even when only tens of probe photons returned after kilometer-scale free-space propagation and scattering from objects.
AI.conclusion: Polarization entanglement remains robust under long-distance free-space propagation and scattering, enabling practical quantum illumination and ranging applications even in lossy environments with minimal photon returns.

title: Cascaded Optomechanical Sensing for Small Signals
summary: We propose a sensing scheme for detecting weak forces that achieves Heisenberg-limited sensitivity without relying on entanglement or other non-classical resources. Our scheme utilizes coherent averaging across a chain of N optomechanical cavities, unidirectionally coupled via a laser beam. As the beam passes through the cavities, it accumulates phase shifts induced by a common external force acting on the mechanical elements. Remarkably, this fully classical approach achieves the sensitivity scaling typically associated with quantum-enhanced protocols, providing a robust and experimentally feasible route to precision sensing. Potential applications range from high-sensitivity gravitational field measurements at the Large Hadron Collider to probing dark matter interactions and detecting gravitational waves. This work opens a new pathway for leveraging coherent light-matter interactions for force sensing.

AI.tldr: Classical sensing scheme achieves Heisenberg-limited sensitivity for weak force detection using coherent averaging in optomechanical cavities without quantum resources.
